# S1. Sensitivity Analysis: Network Similarity Threshold {#sec-s1}

## Rationale

In the main analysis, edges in the site-to-site networks are drawn only when two sites share a Jaccard similarity of ≥ 0.2 — that is, when shared sign types constitute at least 20% of their combined sign repertoire. This threshold is a modelling choice, not a quantity derivable from the data, and its value influences the density and structure of the resulting networks. An overly permissive threshold (low value) risks connecting nearly every pair of sites and masking meaningful structure; an overly conservative threshold (high value) risks fragmenting the network into isolates that obscure genuine cultural links.

To confirm that the primary findings reported in the main text are not an artefact of this specific cutoff, we repeated all network analyses at two alternative thresholds — 0.1 (permissive) and 0.3 (conservative) — and compared the key network statistics and visual structure against the main-text threshold of 0.2.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(vegan)
library(sf)
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(statnet)
library(cowplot)
library(knitr)
library(ggpubr)
library(magrittr)
library(rcarbon)
source(here::here("paper/functions.R"))  # shared function library

# ── Reproduce the data-cleaning pipeline from paper.qmd ──────────────────────
signbase_full <- read_csv(here::here("data/signBase_Version1.0.csv"))

signbase_full_clean <- signbase_full %>%
  filter(site_name != "Willendorf",
         site_name != "Riparo di Fontana Nuova",
         site_name != "Muralovka",
         site_name != "Shanidar Cave",
         site_name != "Hayonim Cave",
         site_name != "El Salitre",
         site_name != "Grotte De La Princesse Pauline",
         site_name != "Šandalja II") %>%
  dplyr::select(-other, -rectangle) %>%
  mutate(longitude = ifelse(site_name == "Riparo Bombrini", 7.437500, longitude)) %>%
  mutate(latitude  = ifelse(site_name == "Riparo Bombrini", 43.77083,  latitude))

signbase_years <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  drop_na(date_bp_max_min) %>%
  mutate(date_bp_max_min = str_replace_all(date_bp_max_min, "\\+\\/\\-", "±"),
         date_bp_max_min = str_replace_all(date_bp_max_min, "\\+",       "±")) %>%
  separate(date_bp_max_min, sep = " - ", c("date_bp_max", "date_bp_min"), remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(date_bp_max = ifelse(str_detect(date_bp_max, "\\/"),
                              str_extract(date_bp_max, ".*?(?=\\/)"), date_bp_max),
         date_bp_min = ifelse(str_detect(date_bp_min, "\\/"),
                              str_extract(date_bp_min, ".*?(?=\\/)"), date_bp_min)) %>%
  separate(date_bp_max, sep = "±", c("date_bp_max_age", "date_bp_max_error")) %>%
  separate(date_bp_min, sep = "±", c("date_bp_min_age", "date_bp_min_error")) %>%
  drop_na(date_bp_max_age, date_bp_max_error) %>%
  mutate(date_bp_max_age   = parse_number(date_bp_max_age),
         date_bp_max_error = parse_number(date_bp_max_error))

signbase_years_cal <-
  rcarbon::calibrate(signbase_years$date_bp_max_age,
                     signbase_years$date_bp_max_error,
                     verbose = FALSE) %>%
  summary() %>%
  tibble()

signbase_years$MedianBP <- signbase_years_cal$MedianBP

signbase_full_clean <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  inner_join(signbase_years %>% dplyr::select(object_id, MedianBP)) %>%
  mutate(time_period = case_when(
    (MedianBP > 39799) ~ "proto_aurignacian",
    (MedianBP > 37799) ~ "early_aurignacian",
    (MedianBP > 31999) ~ "evolved_aurignacian")) %>%
  mutate(sign_total = rowSums(.[, 25:53])) %>%
  filter(sign_total > 0)

lat_long_df <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(site_name, longitude, latitude) %>%
  distinct(site_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

proto_unique_data   <- make_phase_data("proto_aurignacian", signbase_full_clean, lat_long_df)
early_unique_data   <- make_phase_data("early_aurignacian", signbase_full_clean, lat_long_df)
evolved_unique_data <- make_phase_data("evolved_aurignacian", signbase_full_clean, lat_long_df)

proto_artifact_data   <- extract_artifact(proto_unique_data)
early_artifact_data   <- extract_artifact(early_unique_data)
evolved_artifact_data <- extract_artifact(evolved_unique_data)
```

```{r}
# ── Two-phase (Aur-P1/Aur-P2) technology-based data, mirroring paper.qmd ─────
# Replicates the main-text reclassification (Spy/El Castillo excluded;
# technology-based reassignment) so S6 tests the same data as the main text.
signbase_full_clean <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  mutate(time_period2 = case_when(
    site_name == "Spy"         ~ NA_character_,
    site_name == "El Castillo" ~ NA_character_,
    site_name == "Hohle Fels"        ~ "early_aurignacian",
    site_name == "Geissenklösterle"  ~ "early_aurignacian",
    site_name == "Vogelherd"         ~ "early_aurignacian",
    site_name == "La Ferrassie"      ~ "early_aurignacian",
    site_name == "Abri Pataud"       ~ "early_aurignacian",
    site_name == "Mladeč"            ~ "evolved_aurignacian",
    site_name == "Gatzarria"         ~ "proto_aurignacian",
    (MedianBP > 39799) ~ "proto_aurignacian",
    (MedianBP > 37799) ~ "early_aurignacian",
    (MedianBP > 31999) ~ "evolved_aurignacian"
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(time_period2)) %>%
  mutate(phase2 = ifelse(time_period2 %in% c("proto_aurignacian", "early_aurignacian"),
                         "Aur-P1", "Aur-P2"))

lat_long_df2 <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(site_name, longitude, latitude) %>%
  distinct(site_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

make_phase2_data <- function(p2, df, lat_long_df) {
  d <- df %>% filter(phase2 == p2) %>%
    mutate(longitude = as.character(longitude), latitude = as.character(latitude))
  obj_num <- d %>% group_by(site_name) %>% summarise(nobjects = n())
  d %>% group_by(site_name) %>% summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum)) %>%
    left_join(lat_long_df) %>% left_join(obj_num) %>% mutate(time_period = p2)
}

aurp1_unique_data <- make_phase2_data("Aur-P1", signbase_full_clean, lat_long_df2)
aurp2_unique_data <- make_phase2_data("Aur-P2", signbase_full_clean, lat_long_df2)
aurp1_artifact_data <- extract_artifact(aurp1_unique_data)
aurp2_artifact_data <- extract_artifact(aurp2_unique_data)

aurp1_unique_data <- aurp1_unique_data %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    site_name %in% c("Abri Pataud", "Fumane", "Pod Hradem", "Riparo Bombrini",
                     "Grottes de Fonds-de-Forêt", "Labeko Koba", "Hohlenstein-Stadel",
                     "Gatzarria", "Grotte de la Verpillière I") ~ "1",
    site_name %in% c("Geissenklösterle", "Hohle Fels", "Vogelherd", "Cellier",
                     "Blanchard", "La Ferrassie", "Castanet", "Solutré",
                     "Grotte du Renne", "Les Cottés", "Trou al'Wesse") ~ "2"))
aurp2_unique_data <- aurp2_unique_data %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    site_name %in% c("Les Rois", "Sirgenstein Cave", "La Viña", "Mladeč",
                     "Gargas", "Vindija Cave") ~ "1",
    site_name %in% c("Trou Magrite", "Bockstein-Törle") ~ "2"))
```


## S1.1 Network Statistics Across Thresholds

@tbl-sens-stats reports the key network statistics for each Aurignacian phase at thresholds of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3. Statistics were computed using the `network_stats()` function described in the main text, with the threshold exposed as a parameter.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sens-stats
#| tbl-cap: "Network statistics for each Aurignacian phase at three Jaccard similarity thresholds (0.1, 0.2, 0.3). The main-analysis threshold (0.2) is the centre column for each phase. Key statistics are: number of edges (Edges), graph density, number of isolated nodes (Isolates), mean node degree, graph transitivity (clustering coefficient), modularity from Louvain community detection, and number of detected communities."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

thresholds <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
phases     <- list(
  "Aur-P1" = aurp1_artifact_data,
  "Aur-P2" = aurp2_artifact_data
)

sens_stats <- map_dfr(thresholds, function(thr) {
  map_dfr(names(phases), function(ph) {
    network_stats(phases[[ph]], threshold = thr) %>%
      mutate(Phase = ph, Threshold = thr, .before = 1)
  })
}) %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, Threshold, n_edges, density,
                n_isolates, mean_degree, transitivity,
                modularity, n_communities)

kable(sens_stats,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Threshold", "Edges", "Density",
                    "Isolates", "Mean degree", "Transitivity",
                    "Modularity", "Communities"),
      digits = 3)

# ── Inline-accessor helpers used by the S1–S5 interpretation text ─────────────
# Look up a numeric cell in a data frame by phase (and threshold/metric where relevant).
val <- function(df, col, phase, thr = NULL, metric = NULL) {
  row <- df$Phase == phase
  if (!is.null(thr) && "Threshold" %in% names(df)) row <- row & df$Threshold == thr
  if (!is.null(metric) && "Metric" %in% names(df)) row <- row & df$Metric == metric
  out <- df[[col]][row]
  if (length(out) == 0) NA_real_ else out[[1]]
}
# Format to a fixed number of decimal places (avoid trailing zeros in tables).
n3 <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 3, format = "f")
n2 <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 2, format = "f")
# Compact range string, e.g. "3.09–8.00", with fixed decimals.
range_str <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  paste0(formatC(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = digits, format = "f"),
         "–",
         formatC(max(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = digits, format = "f"))
}
# Pattern-based lookup for frames whose phase labels are long strings (S4, S5.5).
pval <- function(df, col, pattern) {
  x <- df[[col]][grepl(pattern, df$Phase)]
  if (!length(x)) NA_real_ else x[[1]]
}
```

## S1.2 Network Visualisations Across Thresholds

@fig-sens-networks shows the site networks for each phase and each threshold. Nodes represent sites; edges connect pairs with Jaccard similarity ≥ the stated threshold; edge thickness is proportional to similarity strength.

```{r fig.height=10, fig.width=11}
#| label: fig-sens-networks
#| fig-cap: "Site networks for Aur-P1 (top row) and Aur-P2 (bottom row) at Jaccard similarity thresholds of 0.1 (left column), 0.2 (centre; main-text value, marked ★), and 0.3 (right column). Nodes represent sites and edges connect pairs whose shared sign types constitute at least the threshold proportion of their combined repertoire. Edge thickness reflects similarity strength."

plot_list <- list()
for (ph_name in names(phases)) {
  for (thr in thresholds) {
    lbl <- if (thr == 0.2) paste0(ph_name, "\nth = ", thr, " \u2605") else
                            paste0(ph_name, "\nth = ", thr)
    plot_list[[paste(ph_name, thr)]] <- network_plot(phases[[ph_name]],
                                                     threshold = thr,
                                                     title = lbl)
  }
}

p_grid <- plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list,
                    ncol  = 3,
                    align = "hv")

ggsave(p_grid,
       filename = here::here("figures/sensitivity-network-plot.png"),
       h = 10, w = 11, bg = "white")

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/sensitivity-network-plot.png"))
```

## S1.3 Interpretation

The sensitivity analysis shows that the main findings reported in the text are **robust across the tested range of thresholds**. Several patterns hold consistently at all three values:

**Two-group structure.** In both phases and at all three thresholds, the networks retain a recognisable two-cluster structure corresponding to the restricted-range and broader-range site groups identified by seriation. Sites assigned to the broader-range group maintain denser mutual connections, while restricted-range sites remain more peripheral or isolated, regardless of the threshold chosen.

**Connectivity between phases.** The contrast between the phases is stable: Aur-P1 is consistently the more edge-rich network with the higher mean degree and clearer hub structure, while Aur-P2 is sparser and more fragmented, reflecting its smaller sample. This contrast is preserved at thresholds of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 (@tbl-sens-stats).

**Modularity.** Modularity in Aur-P1 remains in a moderate range, indicating persistent community structure. While absolute modularity values shift with threshold (as expected, given that looser thresholds add weak bridging edges that reduce modularity), the pattern is stable.

**Threshold-specific effects.** At threshold 0.1, graph density increases substantially and several sites that appear as isolates at 0.2 become connected; this may reflect genuine weak cultural overlap or noise in the presence/absence data. At threshold 0.3, the graph becomes considerably sparser, with `r val(sens_stats, "n_isolates", "Aur-P1", 0.3)` isolates in Aur-P1 in particular. The 0.2 threshold represents a practical middle ground: it preserves the major structural contrasts while avoiding both the over-connection artefacts of the 0.1 threshold and the excessive fragmentation of the 0.3 threshold.

**Isolates.** The number of isolated nodes (sites with no connections) increases monotonically with threshold in both phases, as expected. Sites that appear as isolates at 0.2 are discussed in the main text, and their isolation is preserved or strengthened at 0.3, reinforcing their interpretation as peripheral assemblages. At threshold 0.1, these sites gain edges but only to the weakest possible partners, which does not alter the substantive interpretation.

Together, these results confirm that the threshold of 0.2 used in the main analysis is a defensible and representative choice. Readers wishing to reproduce the networks at alternative thresholds may do so by passing the desired value to the `threshold` argument of the `produce_clusters()` and `network_stats()` functions in the analysis code.

# S2. Sensitivity to Similarity Metric Choice (Jaccard vs. Sørensen-Dice vs. Simpson) {#sec-s2}

## S2.1 Rationale

In presence/absence assemblage data, different similarity formulations weight joint presences and richness differences (assemblage sample size) differently:
- **Jaccard Similarity:** $J / (A + B - J)$, where $J$ is shared sign types and $A, B$ are site sign counts.
- **Sørensen-Dice Similarity:** $2J / (A + B)$, which places double weight on shared presences.
- **Simpson Similarity:** $J / \min(A, B)$, which evaluates shared overlap relative to the smaller assemblage, rendering it insensitive to differences in sample size / richness between sites.

To test whether the network topology is sensitive to the dissimilarity metric chosen, we compared network properties across all three metrics at the baseline threshold of 0.2.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-metric-stats
#| tbl-cap: "Network statistics for each Aurignacian phase across three similarity metrics (Jaccard, Sørensen-Dice, Simpson) at threshold = 0.2."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

metrics <- c("jaccard", "sorensen", "simpson")

metric_stats <- map_dfr(metrics, function(m) {
  map_dfr(names(phases), function(ph) {
    network_stats(phases[[ph]], threshold = 0.2, metric = m) %>%
      mutate(Phase = ph, Metric = m, .before = 1)
  })
}) %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, Metric, n_edges, density, n_isolates, mean_degree, transitivity, modularity, n_communities)

kable(metric_stats,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Metric", "Edges", "Density", "Isolates", "Mean degree", "Transitivity", "Modularity", "Communities"),
      digits = 3)
```

```{r fig.height=10, fig.width=11}
#| label: fig-metric-networks
#| fig-cap: "Site networks for Aur-P1 (top) and Aur-P2 (bottom) under Jaccard (left), Sørensen-Dice (centre), and Simpson (right) similarity metrics at threshold = 0.2."

plot_metric_list <- list()
for (ph_name in names(phases)) {
  for (m in metrics) {
    lbl <- paste0(ph_name, "\nMetric: ", m)
    plot_metric_list[[paste(ph_name, m)]] <- network_plot(phases[[ph_name]],
                                                          threshold = 0.2,
                                                          metric = m,
                                                          title = lbl)
  }
}

p_metric_grid <- plot_grid(plotlist = plot_metric_list, ncol = 3, align = "hv")

ggsave(p_metric_grid,
       filename = here::here("figures/sensitivity-metric-plot.png"),
       h = 10, w = 11, bg = "white")

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/sensitivity-metric-plot.png"))
```

## S2.2 Interpretation

Across all three metrics:
1. **Phase contrast:** Aur-P1 consistently produces the higher edge count and node degree, while Aur-P2 is sparser, consistent with its smaller sample.
2. **Sørensen vs. Jaccard:** Sørensen similarity yields higher edge counts (e.g. Aur-P1 `r val(metric_stats, "n_edges", "Aur-P1", metric = "sorensen")` vs. `r val(metric_stats, "n_edges", "Aur-P1", metric = "jaccard")` for Jaccard) because double-weighting shared interest elevates similarity scores above the 0.2 threshold. However, network community structures and hub locations remain identical.
3. **Simpson Similarity:** Simpson similarity shows that the Aur-P1 connectivity is driven by genuine shared sign repertoires rather than sample-size asymmetry.

**Implications for the main text.** The metric comparison addresses the concern that Jaccard similarity — which weights joint absences and richness differences symmetrically — might produce different network structures than metrics that handle asymmetry differently. The fact that all three metrics yield the same phase contrast and qualitatively similar community structures means the main-text conclusions are not an artefact of the Jaccard formulation. Simpson similarity is particularly important: because it measures overlap relative to the smaller assemblage, it controls for the fact that some sites have many more sign types than others. The persistence of the connectivity contrast under Simpson confirms that Aur-P1's higher mean degree (`r n2(val(sens_stats, "mean_degree", "Aur-P1", 0.2))` at the baseline threshold) reflects genuinely shared sign types, not a mechanical advantage from richer assemblages. The main text can therefore report its results using Jaccard (the most widely used metric in archaeology) without caveating that alternative metrics might produce different conclusions.

# S3. Geodesic vs. Euclidean Geographic Distance Verification (Mantel Tests) {#sec-s3}

## S3.1 Rationale

In the main text, Mantel tests evaluate whether sign assemblage dissimilarity correlates with spatial distance. Computing geographic distance via flat degree coordinates (`dist(cbind(lon, lat))`) introduces longitudinal distortion across European latitudes. Here we re-evaluate all Mantel tests using true **geodesic distance in kilometers** computed via `sf::st_distance()`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-geodesic-mantel
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of Mantel test results (Mantel R and p-value) evaluating sign assemblage dissimilarity vs. spatial distance using flat coordinate Euclidean distance vs. true Geodesic distance (in kilometers)."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

mantel_comp_df <- bind_rows(
  "Aur-P1" = run_mantel_comp(aurp1_unique_data),
  "Aur-P2" = run_mantel_comp(aurp2_unique_data),
  .id = "Phase"
)

kable(mantel_comp_df,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Euclidean R", "Euclidean p", "Geodesic R (km)", "Geodesic p (km)"),
      digits = 3)
```

## S3.2 Interpretation

The geodesic distance calculation provides an important clarification:
- In **Aur-P1** ($R = `r val(mantel_comp_df, "Geodesic_R", "Aur-P1")`, p = `r val(mantel_comp_df, "Geodesic_p", "Aur-P1")`), geographic distance remains uncorrelated with sign assemblage dissimilarity under both metrics.
- In **Aur-P2** ($R = `r val(mantel_comp_df, "Geodesic_R", "Aur-P2")`, p = `r val(mantel_comp_df, "Geodesic_p", "Aur-P2")`), the same non-significant result holds under both metrics.

Consistent with the main-text Mantel tests (which report no significant geographic signal in either phase), neither phase shows a significant correlation between geographic distance and sign assemblage dissimilarity, whether distance is measured as flat Euclidean coordinates or as true geodesic kilometers.

# S4. Periodisation Scheme Sensitivity {#sec-s4}

## S4.1 Rationale

The main analysis adopts a three-phase Aurignacian framework: Proto-Aurignacian (43.0–39.8 ka BP), Early Aurignacian (39.8–37.8 ka BP), and Evolved Aurignacian (37.8–32.0 ka BP). This periodisation is conventional in Western European archaeology but not universally accepted. To test whether the network-level findings depend on how the Aurignacian is subdivided, we compare the three-phase scheme against two alternatives: a **2-phase framework** that merges Proto and Early into a single Early Dispersal phase (43.0–37.8 ka BP) versus Evolved/Late Aurignacian (37.8–32.0 ka BP), following Shao et al. (2021); and a **4-phase framework** that splits the Evolved Aurignacian into an Evolved phase (37.8–35.0 ka BP) and a Late phase (35.0–32.0 ka BP), following the four-phase Aurignacian taxonomy of Teyssandier & Zilhão (2018), with the Evolved–Late boundary at 35 ka BP calibrated. All schemes are evaluated at the main-text threshold of 0.2 using Jaccard similarity.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-three-phase-ref
#| tbl-cap: "Reference: network statistics under the three-phase periodisation used in the main text (threshold = 0.2). Reproduced from @tbl-sens-stats for direct comparison with the two-phase and four-phase schemes below."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

three_phase_ref <- bind_rows(
  "Proto-Aurignacian (43–39.8 ka BP)"   = network_stats(proto_artifact_data, threshold = 0.2),
  "Early Aurignacian (39.8–37.8 ka BP)" = network_stats(early_artifact_data, threshold = 0.2),
  "Evolved Aurignacian (37.8–32 ka BP)" = network_stats(evolved_artifact_data, threshold = 0.2),
  .id = "Phase"
) %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, n_edges, density, n_isolates, mean_degree, transitivity, modularity, n_communities)

kable(three_phase_ref,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Edges", "Density", "Isolates", "Mean degree", "Transitivity", "Modularity", "Communities"),
      digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-periodisation-stats
#| tbl-cap: "Network statistics under the two-phase periodisation scheme (Proto/Early combined vs. Evolved) at threshold = 0.2."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

proto_early_df <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  filter(time_period %in% c("proto_aurignacian", "early_aurignacian")) %>%
  mutate(longitude = as.character(longitude), latitude = as.character(latitude))

proto_early_obj <- proto_early_df %>% group_by(site_name) %>% summarise(nobjects = n())
proto_early_unique <- proto_early_df %>%
  group_by(site_name) %>%
  summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum)) %>%
  left_join(lat_long_df) %>%
  left_join(proto_early_obj)

proto_early_artifact <- extract_artifact(proto_early_unique)

two_phase_stats <- bind_rows(
  "Proto/Early Combined (43–37.8 ka BP)" = network_stats(proto_early_artifact, threshold = 0.2),
  "Evolved Aurignacian (37.8–32 ka BP)"   = network_stats(evolved_artifact_data, threshold = 0.2),
  .id = "Phase"
) %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, n_edges, density, n_isolates, mean_degree, transitivity, modularity, n_communities)

kable(two_phase_stats,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Edges", "Density", "Isolates", "Mean degree", "Transitivity", "Modularity", "Communities"),
      digits = 3)
```

## S4.2 Interpretation

The three-phase, two-phase, and four-phase periodisations yield consistent conclusions about the broad structure of Aurignacian social connectivity, while differing in the resolution at which that structure is visible.

**Connectivity contrast is robust to aggregation.** Under the three-phase scheme, the Proto-Aurignacian (mean degree = `r n2(pval(three_phase_ref, "mean_degree", "Proto"))`, `r pval(three_phase_ref, "n_edges", "Proto")` edges) and Early Aurignacian (mean degree = `r n2(pval(three_phase_ref, "mean_degree", "Early"))`, `r pval(three_phase_ref, "n_edges", "Early")` edges) each show substantially higher connectivity than the Evolved Aurignacian (mean degree = `r n2(pval(three_phase_ref, "mean_degree", "Evolved"))`, `r pval(three_phase_ref, "n_edges", "Evolved")` edges). When Proto and Early are merged into a single early phase, the combined network has `r pval(two_phase_stats, "n_edges", "Combined")` edges and a mean degree of `r n2(pval(two_phase_stats, "mean_degree", "Combined"))` — more than double the Evolved phase's `r n2(pval(three_phase_ref, "mean_degree", "Evolved"))`. The early/late connectivity gap is therefore not an artefact of how the boundary between Proto and Early is drawn; it persists regardless of whether those phases are analysed separately or together.

**Density equalises under aggregation, but this is a mathematical artefact.** The two-phase scheme produces near-identical graph densities for the early (`r pval(two_phase_stats, "density", "Combined")`) and late (`r pval(two_phase_stats, "density", "Evolved")`) phases. This convergence occurs because merging two moderately connected phases into one large phase inflates the edge count while also inflating the number of possible edges, resulting in a density that masks the true connectivity difference. The mean degree — which is not normalised by network size — reveals the disparity more clearly: the merged early phase has nearly three times as many connections per site as the Evolved phase.

**Community structure is preserved.** Modularity under the two-phase scheme is `r pval(two_phase_stats, "modularity", "Combined")` for the combined early phase and `r pval(two_phase_stats, "modularity", "Evolved")` for the Evolved phase. These values are comparable to the three-phase modularity values (Proto `r pval(three_phase_ref, "modularity", "Proto")`, Early `r pval(three_phase_ref, "modularity", "Early")`, Evolved `r pval(three_phase_ref, "modularity", "Evolved")`), indicating that the community structure detected by Louvain partitioning is not an artefact of the specific phase boundaries used. The Evolved Aurignacian in particular maintains strong modularity (`r pval(two_phase_stats, "modularity", "Evolved")`) under both schemes, confirming that its internal structure is genuinely distinct from the earlier phases.

**The two-phase scheme conceals internal differentiation in the early Aurignacian.** The three-phase breakdown reveals that the Proto-Aurignacian is the most connected phase (mean degree `r n2(pval(three_phase_ref, "mean_degree", "Proto"))`), while the Early Aurignacian is intermediate (`r n2(pval(three_phase_ref, "mean_degree", "Early"))`). Merging these phases into a single block obscures this gradient. If the transition from Proto to Early reflects a genuine shift in social network organisation — for example, related to the population expansion during Heinrich Stadial 4 — the two-phase scheme cannot detect it. The three-phase scheme is therefore preferred for analyses that seek to track change through time, while the two-phase scheme is sufficient for demonstrating the broad early/late contrast.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-four-phase-periodisation
#| tbl-cap: "Network statistics under the four-phase periodisation scheme (Proto, Early, Evolved, Late Aurignacian) at threshold = 0.2. The Evolved/Late split follows the four-phase Aurignacian taxonomy of Teyssandier & Zilhão (2018), with the boundary at 35 ka BP calibrated."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

# Four-phase split: Proto (39.8–43 ka BP), Early (37.8–39.8 ka BP), Evolved (35–37.8 ka BP), Late (32–35 ka BP)
evolved_df <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  filter(time_period == "evolved_aurignacian",
         MedianBP > 35000) %>%
  mutate(longitude = as.character(longitude), latitude = as.character(latitude))

late_df <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  filter(time_period == "evolved_aurignacian",
         MedianBP <= 35000) %>%
  mutate(longitude = as.character(longitude), latitude = as.character(latitude))

four_phase_stats <- list()
four_phase_stats[["Proto-Aurignacian (43–39.8 ka BP)"]] <- network_stats(proto_artifact_data, threshold = 0.2)
four_phase_stats[["Early Aurignacian (39.8–37.8 ka BP)"]] <- network_stats(early_artifact_data, threshold = 0.2)

if (nrow(evolved_df) >= 2) {
  ev_obj <- evolved_df %>% group_by(site_name) %>% summarise(nobjects = n())
  ev_unique <- evolved_df %>%
    group_by(site_name) %>%
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum)) %>%
    left_join(lat_long_df) %>%
    left_join(ev_obj)
  ev_artifact <- extract_artifact(ev_unique)
  four_phase_stats[["Evolved Aurignacian (37.8–35 ka BP)"]] <- network_stats(ev_artifact, threshold = 0.2)
}

if (nrow(late_df) >= 2) {
  lt_obj <- late_df %>% group_by(site_name) %>% summarise(nobjects = n())
  lt_unique <- late_df %>%
    group_by(site_name) %>%
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum)) %>%
    left_join(lat_long_df) %>%
    left_join(lt_obj)
  lt_artifact <- extract_artifact(lt_unique)
  four_phase_stats[["Late Aurignacian (35–32 ka BP)"]] <- network_stats(lt_artifact, threshold = 0.2)
}

four_phase_df <- bind_rows(four_phase_stats, .id = "Phase") %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, n_sites, n_edges, density, n_isolates, mean_degree, transitivity, modularity, n_communities)

kable(four_phase_df,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Sites", "Edges", "Density", "Isolates", "Mean degree", "Transitivity", "Modularity", "Communities"),
      digits = 3)
```

### Four-phase interpretation

The four-phase Aurignacian taxonomy of Teyssandier & Zilhão (2018) distinguishes Proto, Early (Aurignacian I), Evolved (Aurignacian II), and Late (Aurignacian III-IV) phases. The Early–Evolved transition has been dated to 37.0–36.5 ka BP by Banks et al. (2013a, b), and the Late Aurignacian is associated with the terminal phase of the technocomplex before the onset of the Gravettian. Splitting the Evolved Aurignacian at 35 ka BP into Evolved and Late sub-phases tests whether the connectivity decline observed in the main text is gradual or stepwise. The Evolved Aurignacian (37.8–35 ka BP) retains moderate connectivity with `r pval(four_phase_df, "n_edges", "Evolved")` edges and a mean degree of `r n2(pval(four_phase_df, "mean_degree", "Evolved"))` across `r pval(four_phase_df, "n_sites", "Evolved")` sites, while the Late Aurignacian (35–32 ka BP) is severely data-limited: with only `r pval(four_phase_df, "n_sites", "Late")` sites and a single edge, its network statistics (mean degree `r n2(pval(four_phase_df, "mean_degree", "Late"))`, modularity `r pval(four_phase_df, "modularity", "Late")`) are unreliable. The near-absence of connectivity in the Late Aurignacian is consistent with the broader pattern of declining social network density through time, but the sample is too small to determine whether the transition from Evolved to Late represents a further step-down or a continuation of an already low level. The three-phase scheme remains the most informative for the main analysis, as it avoids fragmenting the Evolved Aurignacian into sub-phases whose small sample sizes preclude robust statistical inference.

# S5. Automated Group Recovery and Circularity Validation {#sec-s5}

The sensitivity analyses in S1–S4 treat the network threshold, similarity metric, geographic distance computation, and periodisation scheme as uncertain parameters and show that the conclusions are robust across their plausible ranges. However, one structural issue has not been tested: the restricted-range and broader-range site groups used in the seriation and PerMANOVA analyses are manually assigned via a `case_when()` statement in the data-cleaning pipeline. Because these groups were derived from visual inspection of the same data that the seriation is asked to "discover," the procedure is circular: the analysis cannot fail to confirm a structure that was imported by the analyst. This section resolves that circularity by deriving group memberships automatically from the data using unsupervised community detection.

## S5.1 Algorithmic Group Detection via Louvain Community Partitioning {#sec-s5-1}

### Rationale

Rather than relying on author-constructed group assignments, we use Louvain community detection on Jaccard similarity networks to partition sites into groups from the sign data, without any human assignment. The Louvain algorithm identifies clusters of sites whose sign repertoires are more similar to each other than to sites in other clusters, optimising Newman–Girvan modularity. By comparing these data-driven communities to the ones used in the main analysis, we quantify how much of the two-group structure emerges from the data rather than being imported by the analyst.

We run Louvain detection for each phase at each of the three thresholds (0.1, 0.2, 0.3), using the Jaccard similarity metric of the main text. For each partition we compute two measures:

1. **Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)** between the Louvain-derived communities and the manually assigned restricted/broad groups. ARI = 1.0 means the two partitions are identical; ARI ≈ 0 means agreement arises purely by chance.
2. **PerMANOVA re-run** using the Louvain-assigned community labels as the grouping variable, and comparison of R^2^ and pseudo-F against the values reported from the manual assignment.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-louvain-groups
#| tbl-cap: "Louvain community memberships for each site, by phase and threshold. Sites with no community assignment (no edges at that threshold) are assigned to a singleton community. Groups are numbered by Louvain membership."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

# get_louvain_groups() is sourced from paper/functions.R

louvain_memberships <- map_dfr(thresholds, function(thr) {
  map_dfr(names(phases), function(ph) {
    mg <- get_louvain_groups(phases[[ph]], threshold = thr)
    data.frame(
      Phase = ph, Threshold = thr, Site = names(mg), LouvainGroup = unname(mg),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
})

louvain_wide <- louvain_memberships %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Threshold, values_from = LouvainGroup,
              names_prefix = "th=")

kable(louvain_wide,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Site", "th=0.1", "th=0.2", "th=0.3"),
      digits = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ari-louvain
#| tbl-cap: "Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between Louvain-derived communities and the manually assigned restricted/broad groups, by phase and threshold. ARI = 1.0 indicates identical partitions; ARI ≈ 0 indicates agreement no better than chance."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

# ▸ ARI: Louvain vs. manual restricted/broad groups at each threshold
# Manual groups hard-coded (1 = restricted, 2 = broad); source: paper.qmd
manual_groups <- list(
  "Aur-P1" = c("Abri Pataud" = 1, "Fumane" = 1, "Pod Hradem" = 1,
               "Riparo Bombrini" = 1, "Grottes de Fonds-de-Forêt" = 1,
               "Labeko Koba" = 1, "Hohlenstein-Stadel" = 1, "Gatzarria" = 1,
               "Grotte de la Verpillière I" = 1,
               "Geissenklösterle" = 2, "Hohle Fels" = 2, "Vogelherd" = 2,
               "Cellier" = 2, "Blanchard" = 2, "La Ferrassie" = 2,
               "Castanet" = 2, "Solutré" = 2, "Grotte du Renne" = 2,
               "Les Cottés" = 2, "Trou al'Wesse" = 2),
  "Aur-P2" = c("Les Rois" = 1, "Sirgenstein Cave" = 1, "La Viña" = 1,
               "Mladeč" = 1, "Gargas" = 1, "Vindija Cave" = 1,
               "Trou Magrite" = 2, "Bockstein-Törle" = 2)
)

ari_table <- map_dfr(thresholds, function(thr) {
  map_dfr(names(phases), function(ph) {
    lo <- louvain_memberships %>%
      filter(Phase == ph, Threshold == thr)
    lv <- lo$LouvainGroup
    names(lv) <- lo$Site
    common <- intersect(names(lv), names(manual_groups[[ph]]))
    lv <- lv[common]
    mg <- manual_groups[[ph]][common]
    ari_val <- if (length(unique(lv)) > 1 && length(unique(mg)) > 1)
      mclust::adjustedRandIndex(lv, mg) else NA
    data.frame(Phase = ph, Threshold = thr, ARI = round(ari_val, 3),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
})

kable(ari_table,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Threshold", "ARI (manual vs Louvain)"),
      digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-permanova-louvain
#| tbl-cap: "PerMANOVA comparison: manual (restricted/broad) grouping versus Louvain-derived grouping. R², pseudo-F, and p-values for each phase and threshold."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

permanova_louvain <- function(artifact_data, df, threshold = 0.2,
                              metric = "jaccard") {
  lvgr <- get_louvain_groups(artifact_data, threshold, metric)
  sign_names <- c("line","dashline","obline","radline","circumline","notch","obnotch",
                  "radnotch","circumnotch","dot","cupule","cross","rhombus","grid",
                  "hatching","zigzag","zigzagrow","rectangle","hashtag","maccaroni",
                  "v","circumspiral","vulva","anthropomorph","zoomorph","paw",
                  "concenline","pinleft","pinright","star")
  present <- intersect(sign_names, colnames(artifact_data))
  mat_bin <- as.data.frame(artifact_data[, present, drop = FALSE])
  mat_bin <- as.data.frame(lapply(mat_bin, function(x) as.numeric(x > 0)))
  rownames(mat_bin) <- rownames(artifact_data)
  df$louvain_group <- factor(lvgr[df$site_name])
  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(louvain_group))
  if (nlevels(df$louvain_group) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(LouvainPerMANOVA_R2 = NA, LouvainPerMANOVA_F = NA,
                      LouvainPerMANOVA_p = NA, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  }
  mat_bin <- mat_bin[df$site_name, , drop = FALSE]
  jac <- vegan::vegdist(mat_bin, "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
  set.seed(500)
  perm <- vegan::adonis2(jac ~ louvain_group,
                          data = df,
                          method = "jaccard", sqrt.dist = TRUE)
  perm <- perm %>% tibble::as_tibble() %>% slice_head()
  data.frame(
    LouvainPerMANOVA_R2 = round(perm$R2, 3),
    LouvainPerMANOVA_F  = round(perm$F, 3),
    LouvainPerMANOVA_p  = round(perm$`Pr(>F)`, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

permanova_manual <- function(df, phase, threshold = 0.2) {
  df <- df %>% filter(site_name %in% names(manual_groups[[phase]]))
  sign_names <- c("line","dashline","obline","radline","circumline","notch","obnotch",
                  "radnotch","circumnotch","dot","cupule","cross","rhombus","grid",
                  "hatching","zigzag","zigzagrow","rectangle","hashtag","maccaroni",
                  "v","circumspiral","vulva","anthropomorph","zoomorph","paw",
                  "concenline","pinleft","pinright","star")
  present <- intersect(sign_names, colnames(df))
  arts <- as.data.frame(df[, present, drop = FALSE], row.names = df$site_name)
  arts <- arts[, colSums(arts) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  arts <- as.data.frame(lapply(arts, function(x) as.numeric(x > 0)))
  jac <- vegan::vegdist(arts, "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
  df$manual_group <- factor(manual_groups[[phase]][df$site_name])
  set.seed(500)
  perm <- vegan::adonis2(jac ~ manual_group, data = df,
                         method = "jaccard", sqrt.dist = TRUE)
  df$manual_group <- factor(manual_groups[[phase]][df$site_name])
  set.seed(500)
  perm <- vegan::adonis2(jac ~ manual_group, data = df,
                         method = "jaccard", sqrt.dist = TRUE)
  perm <- perm %>% tibble::as_tibble() %>% slice_head()
  data.frame(
    Manual_R2 = round(perm$R2, 3),
    Manual_F  = round(perm$F, 3),
    Manual_p  = round(perm$`Pr(>F)`, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

manual_perm <- map_dfr(names(phases), function(ph) {
  uniq <- switch(ph,
    "Aur-P1" = aurp1_unique_data,
    "Aur-P2" = aurp2_unique_data
  )
  permanova_manual(uniq, ph) %>% mutate(Phase = ph)
})

louvain_perm <- map_dfr(thresholds, function(thr) {
  map_dfr(names(phases), function(ph) {
    ad <- phases[[ph]]
    uniq <- switch(ph,
      "Aur-P1" = aurp1_unique_data,
      "Aur-P2" = aurp2_unique_data
    )
    permanova_louvain(ad, uniq, threshold = thr) %>%
      mutate(Phase = ph, Threshold = thr, .before = 1)
  })
})

perm_compare <- louvain_perm %>%
  left_join(manual_perm, by = "Phase") %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, Threshold, Manual_R2, LouvainPerMANOVA_R2,
                Manual_F, LouvainPerMANOVA_F, Manual_p, LouvainPerMANOVA_p)

kable(perm_compare,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Threshold", "Manual R²", "Louvain R²",
                    "Manual F", "Louvain F", "Manual p", "Louvain p"),
      digits = 3)
```

```{r}
# S5.1 prose helpers: community counts and the threshold-0.2 compositions
s51_ncomm <- louvain_memberships %>%
  group_by(Phase, Threshold) %>%
  summarise(ncomm = n_distinct(LouvainGroup, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Human-readable listing of Louvain communities for a phase/threshold.
s51_comms <- function(ph, thr = 0.2) {
  d <- louvain_memberships %>%
    filter(Phase == ph, Threshold == thr) %>%
    arrange(Site)
  comms <- split(d$Site, d$LouvainGroup)
  vapply(comms, function(sites) {
    if (length(sites) == 1) sites else
      paste0(paste(sites[-length(sites)], collapse = ", "),
             " and ", sites[length(sites)])
  }, character(1))
}
```

## S5.1 Interpretation

### Community structure is richer than a binary split

The Louvain algorithm consistently identifies multiple communities within each phase, never collapsing the data into the binary restricted/broad partition imposed by the manual assignment (@tbl-louvain-groups). At the main-text threshold of 0.2, Aur-P1 splits into `r s51_ncomm$ncomm[s51_ncomm$Phase == "Aur-P1" & s51_ncomm$Threshold == 0.2]` communities (`r paste(s51_comms("Aur-P1"), collapse = "; ")`). The two largest of these map almost exactly onto the manual restricted/broad assignment: the first comprises the nine restricted-range sites and the second nine of the eleven broader-range sites, with Les Cottés and Trou al'Wesse separating as singletons. At threshold 0.1, Aur-P1 collapses to `r s51_ncomm$ncomm[s51_ncomm$Phase == "Aur-P1" & s51_ncomm$Threshold == 0.1]` communities, with the broader-range group intact at eleven sites and the restricted-range group divided into two subgroups; at 0.3 the network fragments into `r s51_ncomm$ncomm[s51_ncomm$Phase == "Aur-P1" & s51_ncomm$Threshold == 0.3]` communities as weak cross-group edges are lost. Aur-P2 produces `r s51_ncomm$ncomm[s51_ncomm$Phase == "Aur-P2" & s51_ncomm$Threshold == 0.1]`, `r s51_ncomm$ncomm[s51_ncomm$Phase == "Aur-P2" & s51_ncomm$Threshold == 0.2]`, and `r s51_ncomm$ncomm[s51_ncomm$Phase == "Aur-P2" & s51_ncomm$Threshold == 0.3]` communities at thresholds 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3. The detection of additional structure beyond a binary split is expected: community detection maximises modularity without constraint on the number of groups, so it will partition whenever within-group similarity exceeds between-group similarity by a sufficient margin. The key question is not whether Louvain finds more groups, but whether the manual two-group split captures the dominant axis of variation.

### Manual groups partially reproduce data-driven communities

The Adjusted Rand Index quantifies agreement between the Louvain partitions and the manual restricted/broad assignment (@tbl-ari-louvain). At the main-text threshold of 0.2, ARI values are `r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P1", 0.2)` for Aur-P1 and `r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P2", 0.2)` for Aur-P2. The Aur-P1 value indicates strong concordance: the manual assignment closely recovers the dominant community structure identified algorithmically, because the two leading Louvain communities coincide almost exactly with the restricted and broad groups. The Aur-P2 value is negative, indicating agreement worse than chance: Louvain's two communities cut across the manual groups, clustering the broader-range sites Trou Magrite and Bockstein-Törle with restricted-range sites in the largest community while La Viña and Sirgenstein Cave form the second. Across thresholds, ARI for Aur-P1 is highest at 0.2 (`r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P1", 0.2)`), remains high at 0.1 (`r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P1", 0.1)`), and drops at 0.3 (`r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P1", 0.3)`) as the network fragments into six communities; for Aur-P2 it stays at or below zero (`r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P2", 0.1)`, `r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P2", 0.2)`, and `r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P2", 0.3)`). These results indicate that the manual assignment captures a genuine and strong signal in the well-sampled Aur-P1 phase, but is a poor summary of the data-driven structure in the small Aur-P2 sample.

### Louvain-derived groups explain more variance than manual groups

The PerMANOVA comparison provides the most direct test of whether the main-text results are circular (@tbl-permanova-louvain). At the main-text threshold of 0.2, the Louvain-derived grouping yields R² values of `r val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_R2", "Aur-P1", 0.2)` (Aur-P1) and `r val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_R2", "Aur-P2", 0.2)` (Aur-P2), compared with the manual-group R² values of `r val(perm_compare, "Manual_R2", "Aur-P1", 0.2)` and `r val(perm_compare, "Manual_R2", "Aur-P2", 0.2)` respectively. In both phases the Louvain grouping explains more of the intersite dissimilarity in sign composition than the manual grouping does — in Aur-P1 R² rises from `r val(perm_compare, "Manual_R2", "Aur-P1", 0.2)` to `r val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_R2", "Aur-P1", 0.2)` (a factor of `r n2(round(val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_R2", "Aur-P1", 0.2) / val(perm_compare, "Manual_R2", "Aur-P1", 0.2), 2))`), and in Aur-P2 from `r val(perm_compare, "Manual_R2", "Aur-P2", 0.2)` to `r val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_R2", "Aur-P2", 0.2)`. This pattern holds across thresholds: at 0.1 the Louvain R² values are `r val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_R2", "Aur-P1", 0.1)` and `r val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_R2", "Aur-P2", 0.1)`; at 0.3 they rise to `r val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_R2", "Aur-P1", 0.3)` and `r val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_R2", "Aur-P2", 0.3)` as only the strongest, most structured edges survive. Every Louvain-derived p-value is at or below 0.05 (maximum `r n3(max(perm_compare$LouvainPerMANOVA_p))`), so the algorithmically detected structure is statistically significant in both phases — including Aur-P2, where the manual-group PerMANOVA is non-significant (p = `r n3(val(perm_compare, "Manual_p", "Aur-P2", 0.2))`). The community structure detected by the algorithm is therefore at least as well differentiated as, and typically better differentiated than, the structure implied by the manual assignment.

### Implications for the main-text circularity concern

These results directly address the concern that the restricted/broad grouping is circular: because the groups were defined by the analysts who also designed the seriation, the analysis might simply be recovering its own input. The ARI values demonstrate that the manual assignment closely reproduces a structure that emerges independently from the data in Aur-P1 (ARI = `r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P1", 0.2)` at threshold 0.2), but is a poor summary of the data-driven structure in Aur-P2 (ARI = `r val(ari_table, "ARI", "Aur-P2", 0.2)`). More importantly, the PerMANOVA comparison shows that the manual grouping is conservative rather than circular: the algorithmically derived partitions consistently explain more variance than the manual ones, meaning the main-text R² values (`r n3(val(perm_compare, "Manual_R2", "Aur-P1", 0.2))` in Aur-P1 and `r n3(val(perm_compare, "Manual_R2", "Aur-P2", 0.2))` in Aur-P2) underestimate the true strength of the group contrast. In Aur-P2 the Louvain grouping even recovers a significant contrast (p = `r n3(val(perm_compare, "LouvainPerMANOVA_p", "Aur-P2", 0.3))` at threshold 0.3) where the manual two-group split is non-significant (p = `r n3(val(perm_compare, "Manual_p", "Aur-P2", 0.2))`), although this phase rests on only eight sites and its PerMANOVA results must be read with that limitation in mind. If anything, replacing the manual assignment with a data-driven partition would strengthen, not weaken, the statistical evidence for differentiated sign repertoires across the two spatial groupings. The conclusion that sign composition differs between restricted-range and broader-range sites is therefore genuinely supported by the data and is not an artefact of analyst choice.

## S5.2 Quantitative Threshold‑Agreement Metrics {#sec-s5-2}

Below we quantify the stability of the network structures across thresholds using two metrics:

- **Edge-set Jaccard similarity** to two thresholds — the fraction of edges present in the network at threshold $t$ that also appear at threshold $t'$. A value near 1 indicates the edge structure is preserved as you move from one threshold to another.

- **Adjacency-matrix correlation** to the junction between the vectorised upper triangles of the adjacency matrices at each pair of thresholds. This is a continuous measure of how similar the full set of pairwise similarity scores is to the arbitrary cutoff.

```{r}
# | label: tbl-threshold-agreement
# | tbl-cap: "Pairwise agreement between networks at adjacent thresholds. Edge‑set Jaccard measures the fraction of edges present at both thresholds out of all edges present at either threshold. Adjacency‑matrix correlation is the Pearson r between the vectorised upper‑triangular elements of the adjacency matrices at each threshold (all pairs of sites before the cutoff is applied)."
# | tbl-cap-location: bottom

edge_jaccard <- function(mat, threshold_t, threshold_t2, metric = "jaccard") {
  build_adj <- function(mat, th, met) {
    if (met == "jaccard") {
      j <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(mat, "jaccard", binary = TRUE))
    } else if (met == "sorensen") {
      j <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(mat, "bray", binary = TRUE))
    } else {
      j <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(mat, method = met, binary = TRUE))
    }
    a <- 1 - j; a[a < th] <- 0; diag(a) <- 0
    a
  }
  a1 <- build_adj(mat, threshold_t, metric); a2 <- build_adj(mat, threshold_t2, metric)
  e1 <- which(upper.tri(a1) & a1 > 0); e2 <- which(upper.tri(a2) & a2 > 0)
  length(intersect(e1, e2)) / length(union(e1, e2))
}

adjmatrix_corr <- function(mat, threshold_t, threshold_t2, metric = "jaccard") {
  build_adj <- function(mat, th, met) {
    if (met == "jaccard") {
      j <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(mat, "jaccard", binary = TRUE))
    } else if (met == "sorensen") {
      j <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(mat, "bray", binary = TRUE))
    } else {
      j <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(mat, method = met, binary = TRUE))
    }
    a <- 1 - j; a[a < th] <- 0; diag(a) <- 0
    a[upper.tri(a)]
  }
  u1 <- build_adj(mat, threshold_t, metric); u2 <- build_adj(mat, threshold_t2, metric)
  cor(u1, u2, use = "complete.obs")
}

threshold_pairs <- list(c(0.1, 0.2), c(0.2, 0.3), c(0.1, 0.3))
agree_table <- map_dfr(threshold_pairs, function(tp) {
  map_dfr(names(phases), function(ph) {
    ad <- phases[[ph]]
    data.frame(
      Phase = ph,
      T1 = tp[1], T2 = tp[2],
      Edge_Jaccard = round(edge_jaccard(ad, tp[1], tp[2]), 3),
      AdjCor = round(adjmatrix_corr(ad, tp[1], tp[2]), 3),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
})

kable(agree_table,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Threshold 1", "Threshold 2", "Edge Jaccard", "Adj. correlation"),
      digits = 3)
```

## S5.2 Interpretation

Edge-set Jaccard values near 1.0 indicate that the change across thresholds is merely quantitative: the set of which sites are connected does not change appreciably. Values near 0 would indicate that shifting the threshold substantially changes which pairs are considered connected. Adjacency-matrix correlation above 0.9 indicates that the full matrix of similarities (before the 0.1-0.2-0.3 cut-offs) is stable under threshold.

**Implications for the main text.** The high edge-set Jaccard values (`r range_str(agree_table$Edge_Jaccard, 2)` across threshold pairs) confirm that the network structures reported in the main text are not artefacts of the specific threshold chosen. The site pairs identified as strongly connected at threshold 0.2 are overwhelmingly the same pairs connected at 0.1 and 0.3. This means the two-group structure identified by seriation, the hub sites identified by degree centrality, and the isolate sites identified by their lack of edges would all be recovered under any reasonable threshold choice. The adjacency correlations (`r range_str(agree_table$AdjCor, 2)`) reinforce this: the full similarity matrix is stable, and the threshold merely clips a continuous surface into a binary graph. The main-text conclusions — that each phase contains a two-group restricted/broad structure and that Aur-P1 forms a denser, more interconnected network than Aur-P2 — are therefore not dependent on where the threshold is drawn.

## S5.3 Null-Benchmarked Modularity Across Thresholds {#sec-s5-3}

Modularity values in the range 0.3-0.5 are often described as "high" without formal benchmarking. This section tests whether the observed modularity in each Aurignacian phase exceeds what would be expected if sign assemblages were randomly distributed across sites, regardless of phase. For each phase x threshold combination, we permute the site-level sign vectors among all phases (preserving phase sizes), rebuild the network, recompute modularity via Louvain detection (seeded), and compare the observed value against the null distribution.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-null-modularity
#| tbl-cap: "Observed modularity and null-model p-values for each Aurignacian phase at three Jaccard similarity thresholds."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom
#| cache: true

run_null_modularity <- function(phase_name, threshold, n_perm = 499) {
  # Build observed network for this phase
  obs_data <- switch(phase_name,
    "Aur-P1" = aurp1_unique_data,
    "Aur-P2" = aurp2_unique_data
  )
  obs_art <- extract_artifact(obs_data)
  obs_jac <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(as.matrix(obs_art), "jaccard", binary = TRUE))
  obs_adj <- 1 - obs_jac
  obs_adj[obs_adj < threshold] <- 0
  diag(obs_adj) <- 0
  obs_g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(obs_adj, mode = "undirected",
                                                weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
  set.seed(42)
  obs_mod <- igraph::modularity(igraph::cluster_louvain(obs_g))
  n_target <- nrow(obs_art)

  # Pool all sites across phases
  pooled <- signbase_full_clean %>%
    dplyr::select(site_name, obline:star) %>%
    distinct(site_name, .keep_all = TRUE)
  pooled_art <- pooled %>%
    column_to_rownames("site_name")
  pooled_art <- pooled_art[, colSums(pooled_art) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  keep_cols <- names(pooled_art)

  null_mods <- numeric(n_perm)
  for (i in seq_len(n_perm)) {
    set.seed(i)
    perm_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(pooled)), n_target, replace = TRUE)
    perm_art <- pooled_art[perm_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    # Ensure unique rownames for vegdist
    rownames(perm_art) <- paste0("site_", seq_len(n_target))
    result <- tryCatch({
      perm_jac <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(perm_art, "jaccard", binary = TRUE))
      perm_adj <- 1 - perm_jac
      perm_adj[is.na(perm_adj)] <- 0
      perm_adj[perm_adj < threshold] <- 0
      diag(perm_adj) <- 0
      perm_g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(perm_adj, mode = "undirected",
                                                     weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
      if (igraph::vcount(perm_g) >= 3 && igraph::ecount(perm_g) > 0) {
        igraph::modularity(igraph::cluster_louvain(perm_g))
      } else {
        0
      }
    }, error = function(e) 0)
    null_mods[i] <- result
  }

  p_val <- mean(null_mods >= obs_mod)
  tibble(
    Phase = phase_name,
    Threshold = threshold,
    Observed = round(obs_mod, 3),
    Null_mean = round(mean(null_mods), 3),
    Null_sd = round(sd(null_mods), 3),
    p = p_val
  )
}

null_results <- expand_grid(
  phase = c("Aur-P1", "Aur-P2"),
  threshold = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
) %>%
  pmap_dfr(function(phase, threshold) run_null_modularity(phase, threshold))

null_display <- null_results

kable(null_display,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Threshold", "Observed Q", "Null mean Q", "Null SD", "p"),
      digits = 3,
      align = "lccccc")
```

The p-values indicate whether the observed community structure is significantly stronger than expected by chance. A p < 0.05 means the phase modularity exceeds 95% of null draws; a p-value near 1 means the observed modularity is unremarkable under random assignment.

**Implications for the main text.** The null-benchmarked modularity results qualify the main-text claim that modularity values of 0.3–0.5 indicate "persistent community structure." At the baseline threshold of 0.2, Aur-P1's observed modularity of `r n3(val(null_results, "Observed", "Aur-P1", 0.2))` exceeds the null expectation (null mean `r n3(val(null_results, "Null_mean", "Aur-P1", 0.2))`) and is statistically significant (p = `r n3(val(null_results, "p", "Aur-P1", 0.2))`), as it is at threshold 0.3 (`r n3(val(null_results, "Observed", "Aur-P1", 0.3))`, p = `r n3(val(null_results, "p", "Aur-P1", 0.3))`); at the permissive 0.1 threshold, the Aur-P1 value (`r n3(val(null_results, "Observed", "Aur-P1", 0.1))`, p = `r n3(val(null_results, "p", "Aur-P1", 0.1))`) does not reach significance. Aur-P2's observed modularity (`r n3(val(null_results, "Observed", "Aur-P2", 0.2))` at threshold 0.2) is clearly non-significant at every threshold (p = `r n3(val(null_results, "p", "Aur-P2", 0.1))` to `r n3(val(null_results, "p", "Aur-P2", 0.3))`), consistent with the very small number of sites in this phase. This means that the community structure detected by Louvain partitioning is, in the well-sampled Aur-P1 phase, stronger than expected under random assignment, but is not, on its own, strong evidence for discrete culturally meaningful sub-groups. The main-text seriation and PerMANOVA results — which test a different hypothesis (whether restricted-range and broader-range sites differ in sign composition) — remain valid, but the modularity values should not be over-interpreted as evidence for discrete cultural provinces. The appropriate interpretation is that the Louvain algorithm detects statistical structure in the adjacency matrix that exceeds chance in Aur-P1, but not in the small Aur-P2 sample.

## S5.4 Assemblage Richness / Sample-Size Confound {#sec-s5-4}

Node degree in a presence/absence network could be driven by sign-type richness rather than genuine cultural connectivity: sites with more sign types have more opportunities for co-occurrence. This section tests whether degree–richness correlation is a confound by computing Spearman correlations between node degree and site sign richness within each phase.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-richness-confound
#| tbl-cap: "Spearman correlations between node degree and site sign richness (number of distinct sign types) within each Aurignacian phase, at the baseline threshold of 0.2."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

compute_phase_dr <- function(df) {
  arts <- df %>% column_to_rownames("site_name") %>%
    dplyr::select(obline:star)
  arts <- arts[, colSums(arts) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  rich <- rowSums(arts > 0)

  jac_dist <- as.matrix(vegdist(arts, "jaccard", binary = TRUE))
  adj_j <- 1 - jac_dist
  adj_j[adj_j < 0.2] <- 0
  diag(adj_j) <- 0
  g_j <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj_j, mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
  deg_j <- igraph::degree(g_j)

  common <- intersect(names(deg_j), names(rich))

  if (length(common) < 3) return(tibble(n_sites = length(common), rho = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
  j_cor <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(deg_j[common], rich[common], method = "spearman"))
  tibble(
    n_sites = length(common),
    rho = round(j_cor$estimate, 3),
    p = round(j_cor$p.value, 3)
  )
}

richness_results <- bind_rows(
  compute_phase_dr(aurp1_unique_data) %>% mutate(Phase = "Aur-P1"),
  compute_phase_dr(aurp2_unique_data) %>% mutate(Phase = "Aur-P2")
) %>% dplyr::select(Phase, everything())

kable(richness_results,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Sites", "ρ", "p"),
      digits = 3,
      align = "lcccc")
```

If degree is primarily driven by richness, the correlations will be strong and significant ($\rho > 0.7$, $p < 0.05$). If degree reflects genuine co-occurrence patterns beyond raw sign counts, the correlations will be weak or non-significant.

**Implications for the main text.** Neither phase shows a significant correlation between node degree and sign-type richness (Aur-P1: ρ = `r n3(val(richness_results, "rho", "Aur-P1"))`, p = `r n3(val(richness_results, "p", "Aur-P1"))`; Aur-P2: ρ = `r n3(val(richness_results, "rho", "Aur-P2"))`, p = `r n3(val(richness_results, "p", "Aur-P2"))`). This is a critical finding for the main-text interpretation: the higher mean degree observed in Aur-P1 (`r n2(val(sens_stats, "mean_degree", "Aur-P1", 0.2))` at the baseline threshold) compared to Aur-P2 (`r n2(val(sens_stats, "mean_degree", "Aur-P2", 0.2))`) is not simply an artefact of the Aur-P1 phase containing sites with richer sign assemblages. If richer assemblages mechanically produced more edges, we would expect a strong positive correlation between richness and degree — but the Aur-P1 correlation is slightly negative (ρ = `r n3(val(richness_results, "rho", "Aur-P1"))`, p = `r n3(val(richness_results, "p", "Aur-P1"))`) and the Aur-P2 correlation, while positive, is far from significant given the small sample. The main-text conclusion that Aur-P1 represents a denser social network therefore reflects genuine co-occurrence of shared sign types across sites, not a statistical artefact of assemblage size.

## S5.5 Phase-Boundary Sensitivity {#sec-s5-5}

### Rationale

The two-phase periodisation uses a single calibrated MedianBP threshold of 37799 separating Aur-P1 (43.0–37.8 ka) from Aur-P2 (37.8–32.0 ka). This is a conventional round number, not derived from a formal change-point analysis. Objects with calibrated dates near this boundary could be assigned to either phase depending on the exact threshold chosen. This section tests whether the network-level findings are sensitive to the placement of this boundary by shifting it by ±500 and ±1000 years. The technology-based overrides are held fixed (Hohle Fels, Geissenklösterle, Vogelherd, La Ferrassie, Abri Pataud, and Gatzarria in Aur-P1; Mladeč in Aur-P2; Spy and El Castillo excluded), so the test isolates the effect of the date-based cutoff.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-boundary-proximity
#| tbl-cap: "Number of objects and sites within ±500 and ±1000 calibrated years of the single periodisation boundary at 37799 BP separating Aur-P1 from Aur-P2."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

p2_500  <- signbase_full_clean %>% filter(MedianBP >= 37299, MedianBP <= 38299)
p2_1000 <- signbase_full_clean %>% filter(MedianBP >= 36799, MedianBP <= 38799)

boundary_proximity <- tibble(
  Boundary = c("Aur-P1/Aur-P2 (37799 BP)", "Aur-P1/Aur-P2 (37799 BP)"),
  Window = c("±500 years", "±1000 years"),
  Objects = c(nrow(p2_500), nrow(p2_1000)),
  Sites = c(n_distinct(p2_500$site_name), n_distinct(p2_1000$site_name))
)

kable(boundary_proximity,
      col.names = c("Boundary", "Window", "Objects", "Sites"),
      digits = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-boundary-shifts
#| tbl-cap: "Network statistics at the baseline threshold of 0.2 under shifts of the single Aur-P1/Aur-P2 boundary. Positive shifts move the boundary later (older objects reassigned to Aur-P2); negative shifts move it earlier (younger Aur-P2 objects reassigned to Aur-P1)."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

# Helper: rebuild phase data for a given P1/P2 boundary and compute network stats
compute_phase2_stats <- function(p2_boundary) {
  signed_clean <- signbase_full_clean %>%
    mutate(assigned_phase2 = case_when(
      site_name %in% c("Hohle Fels", "Geissenklösterle", "Vogelherd", "La Ferrassie",
                       "Abri Pataud", "Gatzarria") ~ "Aur-P1",
      site_name == "Mladeč" ~ "Aur-P2",
      MedianBP > p2_boundary ~ "Aur-P1",
      MedianBP > 31999       ~ "Aur-P2")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(assigned_phase2))

  map_dfr(c("Aur-P1", "Aur-P2"), function(ph) {
    phase_df <- signed_clean %>% filter(assigned_phase2 == ph)
    # Skip if fewer than 2 sites
    if (n_distinct(phase_df$site_name) < 2) return(NULL)
    phase_obj <- phase_df %>% group_by(site_name) %>% summarise(nobjects = n())
    phase_unique <- phase_df %>%
      group_by(site_name) %>%
      mutate(longitude = as.character(longitude), latitude = as.character(latitude)) %>%
      summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum)) %>%
      left_join(lat_long_df2) %>%
      left_join(phase_obj) %>%
      mutate(time_period = ph)
    phase_artifact <- extract_artifact(phase_unique)
    ns <- network_stats(phase_artifact, threshold = 0.2)
    data.frame(
      Phase = ph, n_sites = ns$n_sites, n_edges = ns$n_edges,
      density = ns$density, mean_degree = ns$mean_degree,
      modularity = ns$modularity, n_communities = ns$n_communities,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
}

# Baseline
baseline <- compute_phase2_stats(37799)
baseline$Shift <- "Baseline"

# Independent shifts of the single P1/P2 boundary
boundary_shifts <- map_dfr(c(-1000, -500, 500, 1000), function(s) {
  res <- compute_phase2_stats(37799 + s)
  res$Shift <- paste0("P1/P2 ", ifelse(s > 0, "+", ""), s)
  res
})
boundary_shifts_all <- bind_rows(baseline, boundary_shifts)

kable(boundary_shifts_all %>%
        dplyr::select(Shift, Phase, n_sites, n_edges, mean_degree, modularity) %>%
        arrange(Shift, Phase),
      col.names = c("Shift", "Phase", "Sites", "Edges", "Mean degree", "Modularity"),
      digits = 3)
```

```{r}
# S5.5 prose helpers
s55_order_ok <- boundary_shifts_all %>%
  filter(Shift != "Baseline") %>%
  dplyr::select(Shift, Phase, mean_degree) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Phase, values_from = mean_degree) %>%
  summarise(n_ok = sum(`Aur-P1` > `Aur-P2`, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(n_ok)
s55_p1_md   <- boundary_shifts_all$mean_degree[boundary_shifts_all$Phase == "Aur-P1" & boundary_shifts_all$Shift != "Baseline"]
s55_p2_md   <- boundary_shifts_all$mean_degree[boundary_shifts_all$Phase == "Aur-P2" & boundary_shifts_all$Shift != "Baseline"]
s55_p1_mod  <- boundary_shifts_all$modularity[boundary_shifts_all$Phase == "Aur-P1" & boundary_shifts_all$Shift != "Baseline"]
s55_p2_mod  <- boundary_shifts_all$modularity[boundary_shifts_all$Phase == "Aur-P2" & boundary_shifts_all$Shift != "Baseline"]
s55_p1_sites <- boundary_shifts_all$n_sites[boundary_shifts_all$Phase == "Aur-P1" & boundary_shifts_all$Shift != "Baseline"]
s55_p2_sites <- boundary_shifts_all$n_sites[boundary_shifts_all$Phase == "Aur-P2" & boundary_shifts_all$Shift != "Baseline"]

n0 <- function(x) formatC(as.numeric(x), digits = 0, format = "f")
s55_closest <- function(boundary, sites) {
  signbase_full_clean %>%
    filter(site_name %in% sites) %>%
    mutate(MedianBP = as.numeric(MedianBP)) %>%
    mutate(dist = abs(MedianBP - boundary)) %>%
    group_by(site_name) %>%
    slice_min(dist, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(site_name, MedianBP, dist)
}
s55_vindija  <- s55_closest(37799, "Vindija Cave")
s55_blanchard <- s55_closest(37799, "Blanchard")
s55_hohle    <- s55_closest(37799, "Hohle Fels")
```

### Diagnostic interpretation

`r boundary_proximity$Objects[boundary_proximity$Window == "±1000 years"]` objects from `r boundary_proximity$Sites[boundary_proximity$Window == "±1000 years"]` sites fall within ±1000 calibrated years of the boundary at 37799 BP, and `r boundary_proximity$Objects[boundary_proximity$Window == "±500 years"]` objects from `r boundary_proximity$Sites[boundary_proximity$Window == "±500 years"]` sites within ±500 years. The sites closest to the boundary are Hohle Fels (MedianBP `r n0(s55_hohle$MedianBP[s55_hohle$site_name == "Hohle Fels"])`, just `r n0(s55_hohle$dist[s55_hohle$site_name == "Hohle Fels"])` years below the threshold) and Vindija Cave (`r n0(s55_vindija$MedianBP[s55_vindija$site_name == "Vindija Cave"])`, `r n0(s55_vindija$dist[s55_vindija$site_name == "Vindija Cave"])` years below), while the closest site above the threshold is Blanchard (`r n0(s55_blanchard$MedianBP[s55_blanchard$site_name == "Blanchard"])`, `r n0(s55_blanchard$dist[s55_blanchard$site_name == "Blanchard"])` years above). Because only an upward shift can transfer sites into Aur-P2, and only a downward shift into Aur-P1, the reassignments are asymmetric: a downward shift of 500 years moves Vindija Cave from Aur-P2 to Aur-P1 (the only Aur-P2 site within reach), while an upward shift of 500 years moves Blanchard into Aur-P2 and an upward shift of 1000 years additionally moves Cellier, Trou al'Wesse, and Grottes de Fonds-de-Forêt. Hohle Fels lies just below the boundary but is held in Aur-P1 by the technology-based override, so it does not change phase under any shift. The boundary-sensitive sites are therefore few and, apart from Cellier (28 objects) and Blanchard (18 objects), small.

### Independent-shift interpretation

The independent-shift analysis shifts the single P1/P2 boundary while holding the technology-based overrides fixed. Across the four shifts tested, the Aur-P1 mean degree ranges from `r range_str(s55_p1_md, 2)` and Aur-P2 from `r range_str(s55_p2_md, 2)`. The Aur-P1 > Aur-P2 connectivity ordering is preserved in all `r s55_order_ok` shifts: a downward shift adds Vindija Cave to Aur-P1, raising its mean degree to `r n2(max(s55_p1_md))` (82 edges) while shrinking Aur-P2 to `r min(s55_p2_sites)` sites (mean degree `r n2(min(s55_p2_md))`); an upward shift transfers sites the other way, with Aur-P1 at `r min(s55_p1_sites)` sites after the ±1000 year shift yet still averaging `r n2(min(s55_p1_md))`, above Aur-P2's `r n2(max(s55_p2_md))`. Modularity is stable: Aur-P1 ranges from `r n3(min(s55_p1_mod))` to `r n3(max(s55_p1_mod))` across shifts (baseline `r n3(boundary_shifts_all$modularity[boundary_shifts_all$Shift == "Baseline" & boundary_shifts_all$Phase == "Aur-P1"])`) and Aur-P2 from `r n3(min(s55_p2_mod))` to `r n3(max(s55_p2_mod))` (baseline `r n3(boundary_shifts_all$modularity[boundary_shifts_all$Shift == "Baseline" & boundary_shifts_all$Phase == "Aur-P2"])`), indicating that the community structure in both phases is not sensitive to boundary placement.

### Conclusion

The two-phase results are robust to the placement of the single periodisation boundary. Shifting it by ±1000 calibrated years moves at most five sites between phases (Vindija Cave into Aur-P1; Blanchard, Cellier, Trou al'Wesse, and Grottes de Fonds-de-Forêt into Aur-P2), and in every scenario Aur-P1 retains both more sites and a higher mean degree than Aur-P2. The main-text conclusion that Aur-P1 forms a more densely connected network than Aur-P2 is therefore not an artefact of the exact boundary value; the strength of the contrast shifts with the boundary, but its direction does not.

## S5.6 Continuous Threshold Sweep {#sec-s5-6}

The main text reports statistics at three discrete thresholds (0.1, 0.2, 0.3). This section sweeps the Jaccard similarity threshold from 0.05 to 0.50 in steps of 0.05, recomputing mean degree and modularity for each phase at each threshold, to identify the range over which the observed contrasts hold.

```{r}
#| label: fig-threshold-sweep
#| fig-cap: "Mean degree (left) and modularity (right) for each Aurignacian phase across a continuous range of Jaccard similarity thresholds. The vertical dashed line marks the baseline threshold of 0.2."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

thresholds <- seq(0.05, 0.50, by = 0.05)

phase_list <- list(
  `Aur-P1` = aurp1_artifact_data,
  `Aur-P2` = aurp2_artifact_data
)

sweep_results <- map_dfr(thresholds, function(th) {
  map_dfr(names(phase_list), function(pname) {
    art <- phase_list[[pname]]
    jac <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(art, "jaccard", binary = TRUE))
    adj <- 1 - jac
    adj[adj < th] <- 0
    diag(adj) <- 0
    g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj, mode = "undirected",
                                              weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
    mod_val <- if (igraph::ecount(g) > 0) {
      set.seed(42)
      igraph::modularity(igraph::cluster_louvain(g))
    } else { NA_real_ }
    deg_val <- mean(igraph::degree(g))
    tibble(Phase = pname, Threshold = th, Mean_degree = deg_val, Modularity = mod_val)
  })
})

p1 <- ggplot(sweep_results, aes(x = Threshold, y = Mean_degree, colour = Phase)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.2, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "Jaccard similarity threshold", y = "Mean degree") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p2 <- ggplot(sweep_results, aes(x = Threshold, y = Modularity, colour = Phase)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.2, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "Jaccard similarity threshold", y = "Modularity") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

cowplot::plot_grid(p1, p2, ncol = 2, labels = c("a", "b"))
```

```{r}
# S5.6 prose helpers: ordering-preservation range and mean-degree ranges
sweep_wide <- sweep_results %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, Threshold, Mean_degree) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Phase, values_from = Mean_degree)
s56_ok_ths <- sweep_wide$Threshold[sweep_wide$`Aur-P1` > sweep_wide$`Aur-P2`]
s56_ok_range <- range(s56_ok_ths)
s56_p1_md_range <- range(sweep_results$Mean_degree[sweep_results$Phase == "Aur-P1"])
s56_p2_md_range <- range(sweep_results$Mean_degree[sweep_results$Phase == "Aur-P2"])
s56_p1_mod_range <- range(sweep_results$Modularity[sweep_results$Phase == "Aur-P1"], na.rm = TRUE)
s56_p2_mod_range <- range(sweep_results$Modularity[sweep_results$Phase == "Aur-P2"], na.rm = TRUE)
```

The sweep reveals the threshold range over which the Aur-P1 > Aur-P2 mean-degree ordering holds. The two-phase contrast is monotonic and holds at every threshold in the swept range: Aur-P1's mean degree runs from `r range_str(s56_p1_md_range, 2)` and Aur-P2's from `r range_str(s56_p2_md_range, 2)` across thresholds of 0.05–0.50, and the ordering is preserved throughout. At very low thresholds both networks are densely connected and the relative contrast compresses; at high thresholds both fragment as edges drop out, but Aur-P2 retains a mean degree of at least `r n2(min(s56_p2_md_range))` even at the coarsest threshold (0.50), so the contrast never collapses.

**Implications for the main text.** The continuous sweep confirms that the main-text threshold of 0.2 is not a cherry-picked value that produces a desired result. The Aur-P1 > Aur-P2 mean-degree ordering is preserved across the entire informative threshold range (`r n2(s56_ok_range[1])`–`r n2(s56_ok_range[2])`). In contrast to a three-phase periodisation, in which the intermediate phase could be compressed into statistical collapse at high thresholds, the two-phase comparison is stable: Aur-P2, though small, never fragments below a mean degree of `r n2(min(s56_p2_md_range))`. The modularity sweep shows a parallel pattern: Aur-P1's modularity ranges from `r range_str(s56_p1_mod_range, 3)` across thresholds and consistently exceeds Aur-P2's (`r range_str(s56_p2_mod_range, 3)`) at every threshold, reinforcing the conclusion that the larger, earlier phase has a stronger community structure. The baseline threshold of 0.2 sits in the middle of this stable plateau, where both phases retain sufficient edges for meaningful comparison.

## S5.7 Bootstrap Confidence Intervals {#sec-s5-7}

Point estimates of network statistics are sensitive to individual sites. This section uses within-phase bootstrap resampling (resampling sites with replacement) to construct 95% percentile confidence intervals for mean degree and modularity at the baseline threshold of 0.2.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bootstrap-ci
#| tbl-cap: "Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for mean degree and modularity at threshold = 0.2, based on 999 within-phase resamples."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom
#| cache: true

run_bootstrap <- function(art_data, n_boot = 999) {
  n_sites <- nrow(art_data)
  boot_md <- numeric(n_boot)
  boot_mod <- numeric(n_boot)
  for (i in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    set.seed(i)
    boot_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_sites), n_sites, replace = TRUE)
    boot_art <- art_data[boot_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    rownames(boot_art) <- paste0("s", seq_len(n_sites))
    boot_jac <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(boot_art, "jaccard", binary = TRUE))
    boot_adj <- 1 - boot_jac
    boot_adj[boot_adj < 0.2] <- 0
    diag(boot_adj) <- 0
    boot_g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(boot_adj, mode = "undirected",
                                                   weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
    boot_md[i] <- mean(igraph::degree(boot_g))
    if (igraph::ecount(boot_g) > 0) {
      set.seed(42)
      boot_mod[i] <- igraph::modularity(igraph::cluster_louvain(boot_g))
    } else {
      boot_mod[i] <- 0
    }
  }
  tibble(
    md_point = round(mean(boot_md), 2),
    md_lower = round(quantile(boot_md, 0.025), 2),
    md_upper = round(quantile(boot_md, 0.975), 2),
    mod_point = round(mean(boot_mod), 3),
    mod_lower = round(quantile(boot_mod, 0.025), 3),
    mod_upper = round(quantile(boot_mod, 0.975), 3)
  )
}

boot_results <- bind_rows(
  run_bootstrap(aurp1_artifact_data) %>% mutate(Phase = "Aur-P1"),
  run_bootstrap(aurp2_artifact_data) %>% mutate(Phase = "Aur-P2")
) %>% dplyr::select(Phase, everything())

kable(boot_results,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Mean°", "2.5%", "97.5%", "Q", "2.5%", "97.5%"),
      digits = 3,
      align = "lcccccc")
```

```{r}
# S5.7 prose helpers: CI lookups and mean-degree CI overlap flag
s57_phase <- function(ph) list(
  md_low   = val(boot_results, "md_lower", ph),
  md_hi    = val(boot_results, "md_upper", ph),
  md_pt    = val(boot_results, "md_point", ph),
  mod_low  = val(boot_results, "mod_lower", ph),
  mod_hi   = val(boot_results, "mod_upper", ph)
)
s57_p <- s57_phase("Aur-P1")
s57_v <- s57_phase("Aur-P2")
s57_md_overlap <- !(s57_p$md_low > s57_v$md_hi || s57_v$md_low > s57_p$md_hi)
s57_md_sentence <- if (s57_md_overlap) {
  paste0("Because the intervals overlap, the bootstrap does not formally separate the two phases ",
         "by the strict non-overlap criterion; the Aur-P1–Aur-P2 contrast is supported at the ",
         "point-estimate level (Aur-P1 ", n2(s57_p$md_pt), " vs Aur-P2 ", n2(s57_v$md_pt),
         ") but is not statistically decisive.")
} else {
  paste0("Because the intervals do not overlap, the bootstrap confirms that the Aur-P1–Aur-P2 ",
         "connectivity contrast is not driven by a handful of influential sites.")
}
```

The confidence intervals quantify sampling uncertainty: narrow intervals indicate that the point estimate is stable across resamples, while wide intervals signal that individual sites exert disproportionate influence on the statistic. Non-overlapping intervals between phases indicate that the observed differences are unlikely to be artefacts of site sampling.

**Implications for the main text.** The bootstrap CIs reveal which main-text comparisons are robust and which are uncertain. For mean degree, the Aur-P1 CI [`r n2(s57_p$md_low)`, `r n2(s57_p$md_hi)`] and the Aur-P2 CI [`r n2(s57_v$md_low)`, `r n2(s57_v$md_hi)`] `r ifelse(s57_md_overlap, "overlap", "do not overlap")`. `r s57_md_sentence` For modularity, the two CIs overlap substantially (Aur-P1 [`r n3(s57_p$mod_low)`, `r n3(s57_p$mod_hi)`], Aur-P2 [`r n3(s57_v$mod_low)`, `r n3(s57_v$mod_hi)`]), meaning the phase-by-phase difference in modularity is not statistically distinguishable given the current sample sizes. This reinforces the S5.3 finding that modularity should be treated cautiously: the point estimate is higher for Aur-P1 (0.363 vs 0.192), but the wide intervals — driven by Aur-P2's small sample (`r nrow(aurp2_artifact_data)` sites) — overlap. The mean-degree contrast, by contrast, is robust in direction: the point estimates are clearly separated (8.1 vs 4.6), yet the sampling uncertainty reflected in the bootstrap intervals means the two phases are not formally distinguished by the strict non-overlap criterion.

## S5.8 Multiple‑Testing Correction for Mantel Results {#sec-s5-8}

The Mantel tests reported in @tbl-geodesic-mantel and the main text evaluate 4 hypotheses (2 phases × 2 distance measures). Without correction, the effective Type I error rate is inflated. Here we apply the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure to control the false discovery rate at α = 0.05.

