```{r}
#| label: tbl-mantel-bh
#| tbl-cap: "Mantel test p-values before and after Benjamini–Hochberg correction for multiple testing across 2 phases × 2 distance measures (4 tests total). Results with adjusted p < 0.05 are highlighted."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

# Rerun all Mantel tests and collect results
mantel_all <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(Phase = "Aur-P1", run_mantel_comp(aurp1_unique_data)),
  data.frame(Phase = "Aur-P2", run_mantel_comp(aurp2_unique_data))
)

# Build vector of 4 raw p-values: Euclidean x2 then Geodesic x2
raw_p <- c(mantel_all$Euclidean_p, mantel_all$Geodesic_p)
test_labels <- c(
  paste0("Euclidean – ", mantel_all$Phase),
  paste0("Geodesic – ", mantel_all$Phase)
)
r_vals <- c(mantel_all$Euclidean_R, mantel_all$Geodesic_R)

# Benjamini-Hochberg correction
adj_p <- p.adjust(raw_p, method = "BH")

mantel_bh <- tibble(
  Test = test_labels,
  R = round(r_vals, 3),
  `Raw p` = raw_p,
  `BH-adjusted p` = round(adj_p, 3),
  Significant = ifelse(adj_p < 0.05, "Yes", "No")
)

kable(mantel_bh,
      col.names = c("Test", "R", "Raw p", "BH-adjusted p", "Significant"),
      digits = 3,
      align = "lcccc")
```

```{r}
# S5.8 prose helpers: the closest-to-significance result
s58_best <- mantel_bh %>% arrange(`Raw p`) %>% slice(1)
s58_test  <- s58_best$Test[1]
s58_R     <- s58_best$R[1]
s58_rawp  <- s58_best$`Raw p`[1]
s58_adjp  <- s58_best$`BH-adjusted p`[1]
s58_n_sig <- sum(mantel_bh$Significant == "Yes")
s58_after_text <- if (s58_n_sig == 0) {
  paste0("None of the ", nrow(mantel_bh), " tests reach significance after correction.")
} else {
  paste0(s58_n_sig, " of the ", nrow(mantel_bh), " tests reach significance after correction.")
}
```

Of the `r nrow(mantel_bh)` tests, none approaches nominal significance: the smallest raw $p$-value is `r s58_test` ($R = `r n3(s58_R)`$, raw $p = `r n3(s58_rawp)`$), well above the 0.05 threshold. After Benjamini–Hochberg correction this adjusts to $p = `r n3(s58_adjp)`$. `r s58_after_text` This is consistent with the main-text interpretation: geographic distance does not account for sign distribution in either phase, and the largest correlations are weakly positive for Aur-P1 and weakly negative for Aur-P2. The absence of any spatial signal reinforces the conclusion that the restricted/broad structure within each phase reflects genuine co-occurrence of shared sign types across sites rather than spatial isolation.

## S5.9 Network-Size Normalised Comparison {#sec-s5-9}

```{r}
# S5.9 prose helper: site counts and percentage surplus
s59_pct_more <- round(100 * (nrow(aurp1_artifact_data) - nrow(aurp2_artifact_data)) / nrow(aurp2_artifact_data))
```

Modularity and mean degree are not invariant to the number of nodes: larger networks tend to have higher modularity even under random assignment. Aur-P1 (`r nrow(aurp1_artifact_data)` sites) has `r s59_pct_more`% more nodes than Aur-P2 (`r nrow(aurp2_artifact_data)` sites). This section normalises each metric by its expected value under a size-matched Erdos-Renyi random graph, producing an effect-size ratio that is comparable across phases.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-size-normalised
#| tbl-cap: "Network metrics normalised by size-matched Erdos-Renyi expectation. Ratio > 1 indicates the observed value exceeds the random expectation for a network of the same size. ER mean and SD are based on 100 random graphs per phase."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

compute_normalised_metrics <- function(art, n_rand = 100) {
  jac <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(art, "jaccard", binary = TRUE))
  adj <- 1 - jac
  adj[adj < 0.2] <- 0
  diag(adj) <- 0
  n <- nrow(adj)
  p <- sum(adj > 0) / (n * (n - 1))
  set.seed(42)
  g_obs <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj, mode = "undirected",
                                                weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
  obs_md <- mean(igraph::degree(g_obs))
  set.seed(42)
  obs_mod <- igraph::modularity(igraph::cluster_louvain(g_obs))

  er_md <- numeric(n_rand)
  er_mod <- numeric(n_rand)
  for (i in seq_len(n_rand)) {
    g_er <- igraph::sample_gnp(n, p, directed = FALSE)
    er_md[i] <- mean(igraph::degree(g_er))
    set.seed(i)
    er_mod[i] <- igraph::modularity(igraph::cluster_louvain(g_er))
  }

  tibble(
    Sites = n,
    Obs_md = round(obs_md, 2),
    ER_md = round(mean(er_md), 2),
    MD_ratio = round(obs_md / mean(er_md), 2),
    Obs_mod = round(obs_mod, 3),
    ER_mod = round(mean(er_mod), 3),
    Mod_ratio = round(obs_mod / max(mean(er_mod), 0.001), 2)
  )
}

norm_results <- bind_rows(
  compute_normalised_metrics(aurp1_artifact_data) %>% mutate(Phase = "Aur-P1"),
  compute_normalised_metrics(aurp2_artifact_data) %>% mutate(Phase = "Aur-P2")
) %>% dplyr::select(Phase, everything())

kable(norm_results,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Sites", "Obs. md", "ER md", "MD ratio",
                     "Obs. Q", "ER Q", "Q ratio"),
      digits = 2,
      align = "lcccccccc")
```

The ratio columns (MD ratio and Q ratio) are the key normalised comparisons. A ratio of 1.0 means the observed metric equals the random expectation; ratios significantly above 1.0 indicate genuine structure beyond what node count alone produces.

**Implications for the main text.** The size-normalised results address a potential confound: Aur-P1 (`r nrow(aurp1_artifact_data)` sites) has `r s59_pct_more`% more sites than Aur-P2 (`r nrow(aurp2_artifact_data)` sites), and larger networks mechanically produce higher mean degree and modularity even under random wiring. The Erdos-Renyi normalisation shows that this confound does not drive the main-text results. Mean degree ratios are reported for both phases (Aur-P1 `r n2(val(norm_results, "MD_ratio", "Aur-P1"))`, Aur-P2 `r n2(val(norm_results, "MD_ratio", "Aur-P2"))`), confirming whether the observed mean degrees are consistent with random expectation for networks of these sizes — noting that Erdos-Renyi preserves edge density, so a ratio near 1 does not mean the networks lack structure. The modularity ratios tell the real story: Aur-P1 (`r n2(val(norm_results, "Mod_ratio", "Aur-P1"))`) and Aur-P2 (`r n2(val(norm_results, "Mod_ratio", "Aur-P2"))`) are compared against the random expectation for a network of the same size, so any main-text claim that one phase is more internally structured than the other is evaluated net of the 20-versus-8 site asymmetry rather than as an artefact of it.

# S6. Robustness of the Two-Group Structure: Bootstrap Consensus and Stochastic Block Models {#sec-s6}

## S6.1 Rationale {#sec-s6-1}

The main-text claim that each phase resolves into two cultural groups — restricted-range versus broader-range sign repertoires — rests on a single Brower-Kile seriation run followed by manual block assignment (see S5). Two limitations remain unaddressed by S1–S5. First, the seriation is a deterministic operation on a single observed sample: no quantity is attached to the *sampling uncertainty* of the resulting block structure, so we do not know whether the same two groups would emerge if sites were resampled. Second, group membership is treated as a hard, analyst-assigned label rather than a probabilistic quantity, so borderline sites (e.g. Les Cottés, Trou al'Wesse, Grotte de la Verpillière I) are forced into a single group without an associated measure of confidence.

This section addresses both limitations. In S6.2 we use bootstrap resampling of sites within each phase to build a **consensus co-clustering matrix** (Monti et al. 2003), quantifying the stability of the two-group partition as a whole and of each site's assignment. In S6.3 we fit **stochastic block models (SBM)**, which treat block membership as a latent variable, select the number of blocks via the Integrated Classification Likelihood (ICL), and return posterior membership probabilities for every site. In S6.4 we cross-validate the bootstrap and SBM assignments against the main-text restricted/broad groups using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI).

## S6.2 Bootstrap Consensus Analysis {#sec-s6-2}

### Rationale

For each phase we resample the site-by-sign presence/absence matrix **with replacement** (n = 1000 replicates), recompute Jaccard dissimilarity, and partition the resampled sites into two clusters by Ward-linkage hierarchical clustering on the Jaccard distance. For every pair of original sites we record the proportion of replicates in which the two fall in the same cluster — the *consensus co-clustering probability*. If the two-group structure identified in the main text is genuine, mean co-clustering *within* each block (restricted/broad) should substantially exceed mean co-clustering *across* the two blocks, and sites central to a block should show high per-site consistency (the proportion of replicates in which the site is assigned to its modal block). Low within-block co-clustering identifies sites whose group assignment is not robust to sampling.

```{r}
#| label: s6-boot-functions
# Bootstrap consensus co-clustering into k blocks, from a site x sign matrix.
s6_boot_consensus <- function(mat, n_boot = 1000, k = 2) {
  x <- as.matrix(mat); x[x > 0] <- 1
  sites <- rownames(x); n <- nrow(x)
  co <- matrix(0, n, n, dimnames = list(sites, sites))
  cnt <- matrix(0, n, n, dimnames = list(sites, sites))
  assign <- matrix(0L, n, n_boot, dimnames = list(sites, NULL))
  for (bk in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    set.seed(bk)
    idx <- sample(n, replace = TRUE)
    b <- x[idx, , drop = FALSE]; rownames(b) <- paste0("r", seq_len(n))
    cl <- cutree(hclust(vegan::vegdist(b, "jaccard", binary = TRUE), method = "ward.D2"), k = k)
    for (r in seq_len(n)) assign[idx[r], bk] <- cl[r]
  }
  present <- assign > 0
  for (i in seq_len(n)) for (j in seq_len(n)) if (i < j) {
    v <- present[i, ] & present[j, ]
    cnt[i, j] <- cnt[j, i] <- sum(v)
    if (cnt[i, j] > 0) co[i, j] <- co[j, i] <- sum(assign[i, v] == assign[j, v]) / cnt[i, j]
  }
  # Reference partition obtained by clustering the label-independent consensus
  # matrix; each resample's cluster labels are realigned to this reference to
  # undo the arbitrary label permutation introduced by hierarchical clustering.
  ref <- cutree(hclust(as.dist(1 - co), method = "ward.D2"), k = k)
  names(ref) <- sites
  for (bk in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    idx <- which(present[, bk]); a <- assign[idx, bk]
    agree_id <- sum((a == 1) == (ref[idx] == 1))
    agree_sw <- sum((a == 1) == (ref[idx] == 2))
    if (agree_sw > agree_id) a <- ifelse(a == 1, 2, 1)
    assign[idx, bk] <- a
  }
  modal <- apply(assign, 1, function(v) { t <- table(v[v > 0]); as.integer(names(t)[which.max(t)]) })
  consistency <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    v <- assign[i, ]; v <- v[v > 0]
    if (!length(v)) NA_real_ else mean(v == modal[i])
  }, numeric(1))
  names(consistency) <- sites
  list(consensus = co, partition = ref, modal = modal, consistency = consistency)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: s6-boot-compute
# Main-text restricted(1)/broad(2) groups for the two-phase framework.
s6_groups <- list(
  "Aur-P1" = c("Abri Pataud" = 1, "Fumane" = 1, "Pod Hradem" = 1,
               "Riparo Bombrini" = 1, "Grottes de Fonds-de-Forêt" = 1,
               "Labeko Koba" = 1, "Hohlenstein-Stadel" = 1, "Gatzarria" = 1,
               "Grotte de la Verpillière I" = 1,
               "Geissenklösterle" = 2, "Hohle Fels" = 2, "Vogelherd" = 2,
               "Cellier" = 2, "Blanchard" = 2, "La Ferrassie" = 2,
               "Castanet" = 2, "Solutré" = 2, "Grotte du Renne" = 2,
               "Les Cottés" = 2, "Trou al'Wesse" = 2),
  "Aur-P2" = c("Les Rois" = 1, "Sirgenstein Cave" = 1, "La Viña" = 1,
               "Mladeč" = 1, "Gargas" = 1, "Vindija Cave" = 1,
               "Trou Magrite" = 2, "Bockstein-Törle" = 2))

s6_art <- list(aurp1_artifact_data, aurp2_artifact_data)
names(s6_art) <- names(s6_groups)
set.seed(42)
s6_boot <- lapply(s6_art, s6_boot_consensus, n_boot = 1000)

tri <- function(m) m[upper.tri(m)]
s6_summary <- map_dfr(names(s6_boot), function(ph) {
  cs  <- s6_boot[[ph]]$consensus
  sit <- rownames(cs)
  g   <- s6_groups[[ph]][sit]
  wr  <- mean(tri(cs[sit[g == 1], sit[g == 1]]), na.rm = TRUE)
  wb  <- mean(tri(cs[sit[g == 2], sit[g == 2]]), na.rm = TRUE)
  xr  <- mean(cs[sit[g == 1], sit[g == 2]], na.rm = TRUE)
  nr  <- sum(g == 1); nb <- sum(g == 2)
  ov  <- (choose(nr, 2) * wr + choose(nb, 2) * wb) / (choose(nr, 2) + choose(nb, 2))
  data.frame(Phase = ph, Restricted_n = nr, Broad_n = nb,
             Within_restricted = round(wr, 2), Within_broad = round(wb, 2),
             Overall_within = round(ov, 2), Across = round(xr, 2),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})

s6_site_tab <- map_dfr(names(s6_boot), function(ph) {
  cs <- s6_boot[[ph]]
  data.frame(Phase = ph,
             Site = names(cs$consistency),
             Modal_block = cs$modal,
             Consistency = round(cs$consistency, 2),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bootstrap-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Bootstrap consensus co-clustering within and across the main-text restricted/broad blocks, by phase (n = 1000 resamples). Within-restricted and Within-broad are the mean co-clustering probabilities among site pairs belonging to the same main-text block; Across is the mean co-clustering probability for pairs in different blocks. If the two-group structure is genuine, within-block values should substantially exceed the across-block value."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

kable(s6_summary,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Restricted n", "Broad n", "Within restricted",
                    "Within broad", "Overall within", "Across"),
      digits = 2, align = "lcccccc")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bootstrap-sites
#| tbl-cap: "Per-site bootstrap consistency: proportion of 1000 resamples in which each site is assigned to its modal (most frequent) block. Consistency near 1 indicates robust assignment; values near 0.5 indicate sites whose group membership flips across resamples."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

kable(s6_site_tab,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Site", "Modal block", "Consistency"),
      digits = 2, align = "llcc")
```

```{r fig.height=10, fig.width=9}
#| label: fig-bootstrap-consensus
#| fig-cap: "Consensus co-clustering matrices from 1000 bootstrap resamples of sites within each phase. Cell colour encodes the probability that two sites fall in the same cluster across resamples (1 = always together, 0 = never). Rows and columns are ordered by hierarchical clustering of the consensus matrix. Strong diagonal blocks indicate sites that reliably co-cluster; pale blocks indicate fuzzy, sampling-dependent membership."
#| fig-width: 8

s6_heatmap <- function(ph) {
  cs <- s6_boot[[ph]]$consensus
  hc <- hclust(as.dist(1 - cs), method = "ward.D2")
  ord <- hc$labels[hc$order]
  long <- cs[ord, ord] %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("site1") %>%
    pivot_longer(-site1, names_to = "site2", values_to = "p") %>%
    mutate(site1 = factor(site1, levels = rev(ord)),
           site2 = factor(site2, levels = ord))
  ggplot(long, aes(site2, site1, fill = p)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#FFFFFF", high = "#1F77B4", limits = c(0, 1),
                        name = "Co-clustering") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          legend.key.height = unit(0.9, "cm"),
          panel.grid = element_blank())
}

s6_heatmaps <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  plotlist = lapply(names(s6_boot), function(ph)
    s6_heatmap(ph) + ggtitle(ph)),
  ncol = 1, labels = c("a", "b"), label_size = 14)

ggsave(here::here("figures/bootstrap-consensus-plot.png"),
       s6_heatmaps, width = 9, height = 10, bg = "white")

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures/bootstrap-consensus-plot.png"))
```

### Interpretation

The bootstrap consensus analysis supports the main-text two-group partition as a **coherent, non-random division of the sign data** in each phase, while quantifying how much tighter one block is than the other. In **Aur-P1**, mean within-block co-clustering is `r s6_summary$Within_restricted[s6_summary$Phase == "Aur-P1"]` for the restricted-range block and `r s6_summary$Within_broad[s6_summary$Phase == "Aur-P1"]` for the broader-range block, against `r s6_summary$Across[s6_summary$Phase == "Aur-P1"]` across the two blocks — a strong signal that both groups are internally coherent and sharply separated. In **Aur-P2**, the pattern is `r s6_summary$Within_restricted[s6_summary$Phase == "Aur-P2"]` within the restricted block and `r s6_summary$Within_broad[s6_summary$Phase == "Aur-P2"]` within the broader block, against `r s6_summary$Across[s6_summary$Phase == "Aur-P2"]` across the blocks.

**Per-site stability.** The site-level consistency values (@tbl-bootstrap-sites) show that the strength of the two-group structure is not uniform across sites. Most sites are placed with their modal block in more than 80% of resamples, but a small number are systematically unstable. The least stable sites are the small, low-richness assemblages whose assignment flips across resamples; per-site consistency values in @tbl-bootstrap-sites identify the sites whose block assignment should be read as provisional in the main text. For the reader, the consensus matrices in @fig-bootstrap-consensus provide a direct visual measure of where the two-block structure is tight (dark blocks) and where it dissolves (pale blocks).

**Implications for the main text.** The two-group structure does not dissolve under resampling: within-block co-clustering exceeds across-block co-clustering in both phases, so the broad qualitative claim of a persistent restricted/broad divide is robust to sampling variation. However, the analysis also qualifies the claim: the *strength* of each group differs by phase (and Aur-P2 is far smaller than Aur-P1), and a minority of sites have genuinely ambiguous membership. The main text should therefore present the two groups as a robust but not invariant partition, with per-site confidence available in @tbl-bootstrap-sites.

## S6.3 Stochastic Block Models {#sec-s6-3}

### Rationale

The bootstrap treats block structure as a resampling artefact of an observed partition. The stochastic block model (SBM) takes a different route: it treats block membership as an unobserved latent variable and asks which *generative* model of network structure best explains the observed pattern of sign sharing. In the SBM, the probability that two sites are connected (here: Jaccard similarity ≥ 0.2, as in the main text) depends only on their block memberships. Fitting the model returns (i) the number of blocks that best fits the data, chosen by the Integrated Classification Likelihood (ICL; a penalised likelihood that trades fit against model complexity), and (ii) the posterior probability of membership in each block for every site. Because ICL is a model-selection criterion, the SBM provides a statistical answer to "how many groups are there?" rather than the visual answer provided by seriation.

```{r}
#| label: s6-sbm-compute
s6_sbm <- list()
if (requireNamespace("blockmodels", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(42)
  for (ph in names(s6_art)) {
    x <- as.matrix(s6_art[[ph]]); x[x > 0] <- 1
    adj <- (1 - as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(x, "jaccard", binary = TRUE))) >= 0.2
    diag(adj) <- FALSE
    mode(adj) <- "integer"
    bm <- blockmodels::BM_bernoulli("SBM", adj, verbosity = 0,
                                    explore_min = 1, exploration_factor = 1.5)
    bm$estimate()
    icl <- as.numeric(bm$ICL)
    bestK <- which.max(replace(icl, is.na(icl), -Inf))
    # blockmodels stores the n x K posterior membership matrix Z in the
    # environment of the S4 SBM object corresponding to the chosen K.
    obj <- bm$memberships[[min(bestK, length(bm$memberships))]]
    Z <- slot(obj, ".xData")$Z
    colnames(Z) <- paste0("Block", seq_len(ncol(Z)))
    rownames(Z) <- rownames(x)
    s6_sbm[[ph]] <- list(icl = icl, bestK = bestK, Z = Z)
  }
}
# ── Inline-accessor helpers for the S6.3/S6.4 interpretation text ────────────
# Number of blocks selected by ICL; maximum ICL; ICL gap between the best and
# second-best model; lowest modal-block posterior across sites.
s6_bestK   <- function(ph) if (ph %in% names(s6_sbm)) s6_sbm[[ph]]$bestK else NA_integer_
s6_maxICL  <- function(ph) if (ph %in% names(s6_sbm)) max(s6_sbm[[ph]]$icl, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
s6_gap     <- function(ph) if (ph %in% names(s6_sbm)) {
  v <- sort(s6_sbm[[ph]]$icl, decreasing = TRUE)
  if (length(v) >= 2) v[1] - v[2] else NA_real_
} else NA_real_
s6_minPost <- function(ph) if (ph %in% names(s6_sbm)) min(apply(s6_sbm[[ph]]$Z, 1, max)) else NA_real_
s6_global_minPost <- if (length(s6_sbm)) min(sapply(names(s6_sbm), s6_minPost)) else NA_real_
# Sites whose aligned SBM modal block (SBM block labels optimally remapped onto
# the manual restricted/broad labels) differs from the manual group.
s6_mismatch <- function(ph) {
  if (!length(s6_sbm) || !ph %in% names(s6_sbm)) return(character())
  sit <- names(s6_boot[[ph]]$consistency)
  m   <- s6_groups[[ph]][sit]
  nm  <- apply(s6_sbm[[ph]]$Z[sit, , drop = FALSE], 1, which.max)
  K <- max(nm); best_agree <- -1; best_map <- rep(1L, K)
  for (code in 0:(2^K - 1)) {
    mp <- ((code %/% (2^(0:(K-1)))) %% 2) + 1L
    agree <- sum(mp[nm] == as.integer(m))
    if (agree > best_agree) { best_agree <- agree; best_map <- mp }
  }
  names(m)[best_map[nm] != as.integer(m)]
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sbm-icl
#| tbl-cap: "Integrated Classification Likelihood (ICL) for stochastic block models with K = 1 to 5 blocks, by phase. The best-supported number of blocks (maximum ICL) is bolded. A decisive maximum (large gap in ICL) indicates that the number of groups is well determined by the data; a flat ICL profile indicates the number of groups is weakly constrained."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

if (length(s6_sbm)) {
  maxK <- max(vapply(s6_sbm, function(z) length(z$icl), integer(1)))
  icl_tab <- map_dfr(names(s6_sbm), function(ph) {
    z <- s6_sbm[[ph]]
    data.frame(Phase = ph, K = seq_along(z$icl), ICL = round(z$icl, 1))
  }) %>%
    filter(K <= maxK) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = K, values_from = ICL, names_prefix = "K = ")
  best_ks <- sapply(s6_sbm, function(z) z$bestK)
  icl_tab$`Best K` <- NA_real_
  for (ph in names(best_ks)) {
    icl_tab$`Best K`[icl_tab$Phase == ph] <- best_ks[[ph]]
  }
  kable(icl_tab, col.names = c("Phase", paste0("K = ", seq_len(maxK)), "Best K"),
        digits = 1, align = "lcccccc")
} else {
  cat("S6.3 requires the `blockmodels` package. Run `renv::install(\"blockmodels\")` and re-render.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sbm-membership
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior block-membership probabilities and modal (hard) assignment from the best-fitting stochastic block model for each phase. Probabilities are rounded; the modal block is the column with the highest probability. Sites with probability spread across blocks (e.g. no entry above 0.7) have ambiguous membership."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

if (length(s6_sbm)) {
  s6_mem_tab <- map_dfr(names(s6_sbm), function(ph) {
    z <- s6_sbm[[ph]]
    m <- as.data.frame(z$Z)
    m$Site <- rownames(z$Z)
    m$Phase <- ph
    m$Modal <- apply(z$Z, 1, which.max)
    m %>% dplyr::select(Phase, Site, Modal, everything())
  })
  kable(s6_mem_tab,
        col.names = c("Phase", "Site", "Modal block",
                      paste0("P(", gsub("Block", "B", names(s6_mem_tab)[4:(ncol(s6_mem_tab))]), ")")),
        digits = 2, align = "llc")
} else {
  cat("S6.3 requires the `blockmodels` package. Run `renv::install(\"blockmodels\")` and re-render.")
}
```

### Interpretation

The ICL model-selection results (@tbl-sbm-icl) report the number of blocks best supported by the sign-sharing network in each phase, providing a model-based counterpart to the seriation. In **Aur-P1** the best-supported model contains `r s6_bestK("Aur-P1")` blocks, and in **Aur-P2** it contains `r s6_bestK("Aur-P2")` blocks. The ICL gap between the best and second-best model quantifies how decisively the optimum is preferred (`r n2(s6_gap("Aur-P1"))` in Aur-P1 and `r n2(s6_gap("Aur-P2"))` in Aur-P2); the comparison between the two phases tells the reader how much more strongly the block structure is determined in the better-sampled early phase.

The membership table (@tbl-sbm-membership) gives posterior probabilities that qualify the deterministic group assignments used in the main text: every site is assigned to its modal block with posterior probability ≥ `r n2(s6_global_minPost)`, so the SBM is never equivocal about the partition it identifies, and the informative quantity is the number of blocks chosen and how those blocks map onto the manual restricted/broad groups rather than the confidence of individual assignments. After aligning each SBM block to the nearest manual group, the SBM partition reproduces the manual restricted/broad split exactly in **Aur-P2**, and diverges on `r length(s6_mismatch("Aur-P1"))` of `r nrow(s6_sbm[["Aur-P1"]]$Z)` sites in **Aur-P1** (`r paste(s6_mismatch("Aur-P1"), collapse = ", ")`). Where the number of blocks matches the seriation's two-group structure and posterior probabilities are high, the two-group claim is independently corroborated by a generative model that was never shown the seriation solution. Where the SBM favours a different number of blocks, or assigns low posterior probability to specific sites, the main text should report those sites' membership as uncertain and note that the seriation's two-group simplification captures the dominant but not the complete structure.

**Implications for the main text.** The SBM posterior probabilities are effectively certain (each site's modal block receives posterior ≥ `r n2(s6_global_minPost)`) for the partition the model identifies, so the model is rarely equivocal about its own grouping; the important information lies in *how many* blocks the model chooses and how far that partition diverges from the manual restricted/broad assignment. Where the SBM settles on two blocks and its partition agrees with the manual groups (as in Aur-P2), the two-group structure is independently corroborated. Where the SBM favours more blocks — or partitions sites differently (quantified as ARI in S6.4) — the restricted/broad dichotomy should be read as the dominant axis of variation rather than the complete structure. These results complement, rather than supersede, the bootstrap analysis: the bootstrap quantifies sampling stability of the main-text partition, while the SBM asks whether an independent generative model reproduces it.

## S6.4 Cross-Validation of Group Assignments (ARI) {#sec-s6-4}

### Rationale

To quantify overall agreement among the three ways of partitioning sites — the main-text manual restricted/broad groups, the bootstrap modal blocks (S6.2), and the SBM modal assignments (S6.3) — we compute the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between each pair of partitions for each phase. ARI = 1 indicates identical partitions, 0 indicates agreement no better than chance. We use a self-contained implementation of ARI (the S5 analyses use `mclust::adjustedRandIndex`, which yields the same values).

```{r}
#| label: s6-ari
s6_ari <- function(a, b) {
  a <- as.integer(a); b <- as.integer(b)
  n <- length(a)
  tab <- table(a, b)
  ni <- rowSums(tab); nj <- colSums(tab)
  comb2 <- function(x) sum(choose(x, 2))
  N <- sum(tab)
  (sum(choose(as.vector(tab), 2)) - (comb2(ni) * comb2(nj)) / choose(N, 2)) /
    (0.5 * (comb2(ni) + comb2(nj)) - (comb2(ni) * comb2(nj)) / choose(N, 2))
}

s6_ari_tab <- map_dfr(names(s6_boot), function(ph) {
  sit <- names(s6_boot[[ph]]$consistency)
  manual <- s6_groups[[ph]][sit]
  boot_m <- s6_boot[[ph]]$modal[names(manual)]
  sbm_m  <- if (length(s6_sbm) && ph %in% names(s6_sbm))
    apply(s6_sbm[[ph]]$Z[sit, , drop = FALSE], 1, which.max) else NULL
  row <- data.frame(Phase = ph,
                    ARI_manual_boot  = round(s6_ari(manual, boot_m), 2))
  if (!is.null(sbm_m)) {
    row$ARI_manual_sbm  <- round(s6_ari(manual, sbm_m), 2)
    row$ARI_boot_sbm    <- round(s6_ari(boot_m, sbm_m), 2)
  } else {
    row$ARI_manual_sbm <- NA; row$ARI_boot_sbm <- NA
  }
  row
})

# Cell lookup for the ARI table, e.g. s6_ari_val("Evolved Aurignacian", "ARI_manual_sbm").
s6_ari_val <- function(ph, col) s6_ari_tab[[col]][s6_ari_tab$Phase == ph]
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s6-ari
#| tbl-cap: "Adjusted Rand Index between the main-text manual restricted/broad assignment, the bootstrap modal blocks (S6.2), and the SBM modal assignments (S6.3), by phase. Values are blank for SBM comparisons when the `blockmodels` package is unavailable."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

kable(s6_ari_tab,
      col.names = c("Phase", "ARI manual vs bootstrap", "ARI manual vs SBM", "ARI bootstrap vs SBM"),
      digits = 2, align = "lccc")
```

### Interpretation

The ARI values summarise how far the three routes to the two-group partition agree, and the agreement is informative precisely because it varies by phase and method (@tbl-s6-ari). A high ARI between the manual groups and an unsupervised partition (SBM or bootstrap) indicates that the main-text grouping is not merely an analyst construction but is recoverable from the data. A low ARI indicates a genuine divergence: the manual restricted/broad split and the partition recovered by an unsupervised method organise the sites differently. Because the restricted/broad divide is defined partly by sign-type *richness* (the restricted sites are assemblages with few sign types), it is not in general expected to coincide with clusters defined purely by compositional *similarity*, and low ARI between the manual groups and similarity-based partitions should be interpreted in that light rather than as evidence that either partition is wrong. The specific pattern — which method agrees with the manual groups in which phase — is reported in @tbl-s6-ari and should be used in the main text to state precisely where the two-group structure is independently supported and where it is a simplifying summary.

**Implications for the main text.** The two-group claim should be presented as strongest where the manual assignment, the bootstrap, and the SBM converge, and qualified where they diverge. Where the SBM's best partition reproduces the manual groups (high ARI), the main text can cite the SBM as an independent, model-based confirmation that never saw the seriation solution. Where it does not, the divergence should be acknowledged and the seriation's two-group structure presented as the dominant axis of variation rather than an exhaustive description of the data.

## S6.5 Summary of Implications {#sec-s6-5}

Taken together, S6 provides three converging but graded lines of evidence for the main-text two-group claim. (1) **Resampling stability**: within-block co-clustering exceeds across-block co-clustering in every phase (@fig-bootstrap-consensus, @tbl-bootstrap-summary), so the partition does not arise from a particular sample of sites. (2) **Model selection**: the SBM attaches posterior probabilities to each site's membership (@tbl-sbm-membership) and reports the number of blocks best supported by the sign-sharing network in each phase (@tbl-sbm-icl). (3) **Cross-validation**: ARI between the manual, bootstrap, and SBM partitions quantifies their agreement (@tbl-s6-ari). The three routes are mutually supportive but not redundant: the bootstrap shows the two blocks to be internally coherent and well separated, while agreement between the manual restricted/broad assignment and the partitions recovered by unsupervised methods is phase-dependent. We recommend that the main text retain the two-group framing but cite the per-site consistency scores (@tbl-bootstrap-sites) and SBM posterior probabilities (@tbl-sbm-membership) for the borderline sites, and note that the strength of the dichotomy is phase-dependent and that the Aur-P2 results rest on only 8 sites.

# S7. Object-Type Sensitivity: Figurine Exclusion {#sec-s7}

## S7.1 Rationale

Bentz and Dutkiewicz (2026) demonstrate that ivory figurines in the Swabian Aurignacian carry sign sequences with higher information density than tools. If figurines encode different sign repertoires than other object types, their inclusion could bias site-level sign assemblages — particularly at Vogelherd, where 50 of the dataset's 63 figurines are concentrated. This section tests whether the main-text network findings are robust to the exclusion of figurines, both globally and site-specifically.

## S7.2 Figurine Distribution in the Dataset

```{r}
#| label: tbl-figurine-count
#| tbl-cap: "Distribution of figurine objects across phases and sites. Figurine types include figurine zoomorph, figurine anthropomorph, figurine undet., and possible figurine."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

figurine_types <- c("figurine zoomorph", "figurine anthropomorph",
                    "figurine undet.", "possible figurine")

figurine_summary <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  filter(object_type %in% figurine_types) %>%
  count(phase2, site_name, object_type) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = object_type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) %>%
  arrange(phase2, desc(Total))

kable(figurine_summary,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Site",
                    grep("figurine", names(figurine_summary), value = TRUE, invert = FALSE),
                    "Total"),
      digits = 0)
```

@tbl-figurine-count shows that figurines are heavily concentrated at Vogelherd (50 objects), with minor representation at Hohle Fels (8), Geissenklösterle (3), Hohlenstein-Stadel (1), and La Ferrassie (1). All 63 figurines fall within Aur-P1. The analysis therefore tests whether the Aur-P1 network structure — which reports the higher mean degree (7.50) — is driven by these 50 objects at a single site.

## S7.3 Analysis 1: Exclude All Figurines

### Method

We remove all objects where `object_type` contains "figurine" (63 objects total: 25 zoomorph, 10 undetermined, 5 anthropomorph, 23 possible figurine) from the full cleaned dataset, recompute site-level sign matrices by summing remaining objects per site, and rebuild networks at the baseline threshold of 0.2.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-exclude-figurines
#| tbl-cap: "Network statistics before and after excluding all figurine objects (figurine zoomorph, figurine anthropomorph, figurine undet., and possible figurine). Threshold = 0.2, Jaccard similarity."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

# Baseline stats (already computed)
baseline_stats <- bind_rows(
  network_stats(aurp1_artifact_data) %>% mutate(Phase = "Aur-P1"),
  network_stats(aurp2_artifact_data) %>% mutate(Phase = "Aur-P2")
) %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, n_sites, n_edges, density, mean_degree, transitivity, modularity) %>%
  mutate(Condition = "All objects")

# Helper: rebuild phase data and compute network stats for a filtered dataset
s7_phase_stats <- function(df, condition) {
  map_dfr(c("Aur-P1", "Aur-P2"), function(ph) {
    ph_df <- df %>% filter(phase2 == ph)
    if (n_distinct(ph_df$site_name) < 2) return(NULL)
    lat_long <- df %>% dplyr::select(site_name, longitude, latitude) %>%
      distinct(site_name, .keep_all = TRUE)
    ph_obj <- ph_df %>% group_by(site_name) %>% summarise(nobjects = n())
    ph_unique <- ph_df %>%
      group_by(site_name) %>%
      mutate(longitude = as.character(longitude), latitude = as.character(latitude)) %>%
      summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum)) %>%
      left_join(lat_long) %>%
      left_join(ph_obj) %>%
      mutate(time_period = ph)
    ph_art <- extract_artifact(ph_unique)
    ns <- network_stats(ph_art, threshold = 0.2)
    data.frame(Phase = ph, n_sites = ns$n_sites, n_edges = ns$n_edges,
               density = ns$density, mean_degree = ns$mean_degree,
               transitivity = ns$transitivity, modularity = ns$modularity,
               Condition = condition, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
}

# Exclude figurines
signbase_no_fig <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  filter(!object_type %in% figurine_types)

no_fig_stats <- s7_phase_stats(signbase_no_fig, "Excluding figurines")

# Sites lost
sites_before <- signbase_full_clean %>% count(phase2, site_name) %>%
  group_by(phase2) %>% summarise(sites = n(), .groups = "drop")
sites_after <- signbase_no_fig %>% count(phase2, site_name) %>%
  group_by(phase2) %>% summarise(sites = n(), .groups = "drop")
sites_lost <- sites_before %>%
  left_join(sites_after, by = "phase2", suffix = c("_before", "_after")) %>%
  mutate(lost = sites_before - sites_after) %>%
  rename(Phase = phase2)

excl_comparison <- bind_rows(baseline_stats, no_fig_stats)

kable(excl_comparison,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Sites", "Edges", "Density", "Mean degree",
                    "Transitivity", "Modularity", "Condition"),
      digits = 3,
      align = "llcccccc")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-figurine-sites-lost
#| tbl-cap: "Number of sites per phase before and after figurine exclusion. Sites are lost when all objects at that site are figurines."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

kable(sites_lost %>% dplyr::select(Phase, sites_before, sites_after, lost),
      col.names = c("Phase", "Sites (all)", "Sites (no figurines)", "Sites lost"),
      digits = 0)
```

### Interpretation

Excluding all 63 figurines has no effect on the Aur-P1 network: mean degree is unchanged (7.50 → 7.50), all 75 edges are retained, and no sites are lost (all 20 sites retained). Aur-P2, which contains no figurines, is unchanged by construction (mean degree 4.25, 17 edges, 8 sites). The only detectable effects are small declines in Aur-P1's transitivity (0.711 → 0.699) and modularity (0.332 → 0.324), indicating that figurines contribute modestly to community cohesion but do not create the communities themselves.

Critically, Aur-P1 retains the higher mean degree (7.50) under figurine exclusion, preserving the main-text ordering Aur-P1 > Aur-P2 (7.50 > 4.25). The Aur-P1 network remains the more connected regardless of figurine inclusion, confirming that its structure is not contingent on figurine-bearing sign assemblages at Vogelherd.

## S7.4 Analysis 2: Exclude Vogelherd Figurines Only

### Method

Rather than removing all figurines globally, this analysis removes only the 50 figurines from Vogelherd — the site where figurines are most concentrated — while retaining figurines at other sites. This tests whether the Aur-P1 network structure is driven by a single outlier assemblage.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-vogelherd-exclude
#| tbl-cap: "Network statistics before and after excluding figurines from Vogelherd only. All other figurines (Hohle Fels, Geissenklösterle, Hohlenstein-Stadel, La Ferrassie) are retained. Threshold = 0.2, Jaccard similarity."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

signbase_no_vog <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  filter(!(site_name == "Vogelherd" & object_type %in% figurine_types))

no_vog_stats <- s7_phase_stats(signbase_no_vog, "Excl. Vogelherd figurines")

# Vogelherd object counts
vog_before <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  filter(site_name == "Vogelherd") %>%
  count(phase2, name = "objects_before")
vog_after <- signbase_no_vog %>%
  filter(site_name == "Vogelherd") %>%
  count(phase2, name = "objects_after")
vog_summary <- vog_before %>%
  left_join(vog_after, by = "phase2") %>%
  mutate(removed = objects_before - objects_after) %>%
  rename(Phase = phase2)

vog_comparison <- bind_rows(baseline_stats, no_vog_stats)

kable(vog_comparison,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Sites", "Edges", "Density", "Mean degree",
                    "Transitivity", "Modularity", "Condition"),
      digits = 3,
      align = "llcccccc")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-vogelherd-objects
#| tbl-cap: "Vogelherd object counts before and after removing figurines. Non-figurine objects at Vogelherd (tools, plaquettes, etc.) are retained."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

kable(vog_summary %>% dplyr::select(Phase, objects_before, objects_after, removed),
      col.names = c("Phase", "Objects (all)", "Objects (no figurines)", "Removed"),
      digits = 0)
```

### Interpretation

Removing only Vogelherd's figurines (50 objects: 173 → 123 in Aur-P1) has a negligible effect on Aur-P1: mean degree drops from 7.50 to 7.40 (−1.3%), one edge is lost (75 → 74), and modularity decreases from 0.332 to 0.328. Aur-P2 shows no change whatsoever (mean degree 4.25 → 4.25, modularity 0.125 → 0.125), confirming that Vogelherd figurines do not contribute to network structure in the later phase.

The effect of removing Vogelherd figurines alone (−1.3% in Aur-P1) is comparable to removing all 63 figurines globally (0%), and in both cases the network is essentially unchanged. The figurine effect therefore does not scale with the number of figurines removed; figurines at Hohle Fels (8), Geissenklösterle (3), Hohlenstein-Stadel (1), and La Ferrassie (1) do not alter the network structure, and Vogelherd's connectivity within Aur-P1 is carried by its 123 non-figurine objects.

## S7.5 Joint Comparison

```{r}
#| label: tbl-objtype-joint
#| tbl-cap: "Side-by-side comparison of network statistics across all conditions: baseline (all objects), exclude all figurines, and exclude Vogelherd figurines only. The rightmost columns show the percentage change in mean degree from baseline."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

all_conditions <- bind_rows(
  baseline_stats %>% mutate(Condition = "Baseline (all objects)"),
  no_fig_stats %>% mutate(Condition = "Exclude all figurines"),
  no_vog_stats %>% mutate(Condition = "Exclude Vogelherd figurines")
) %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, Condition, n_sites, n_edges, mean_degree, transitivity, modularity)

# Compute % change from baseline
baseline_md <- baseline_stats %>% dplyr::select(Phase, Baseline_md = mean_degree)
joint_comparison <- all_conditions %>%
  left_join(baseline_md, by = "Phase") %>%
  mutate(pct_change_md = round((mean_degree - Baseline_md) / Baseline_md * 100, 1)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Baseline_md)

kable(joint_comparison,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Condition", "Sites", "Edges", "Mean degree",
                    "Transitivity", "Modularity", "Δ mean° (%)"),
      digits = 3,
      align = "lllccccc")
```

## S7.6 Interpretation

The joint comparison in @tbl-objtype-joint shows that figurine exclusion has a modest and phase-dependent effect on network structure:

| Phase | Baseline mean° | No figurines | Δ | Vogelherd only | Δ |
|-------|---------------|-------------|---|----------------|---|
| Aur-P1 | 7.50 | 7.50 | 0% | 7.40 | −1.3% |
| Aur-P2 | 4.25 | 4.25 | 0% | 4.25 | 0% |

**Outcome observed: Negligible effect, no qualitative change.** Mean degree changes are at most −1.3% across both phases and all conditions, and excluding all figurines leaves Aur-P1's edge set completely unchanged (75 edges, mean degree 7.50). Modularity decreases slightly for Aur-P1 when figurines are excluded (0.332 → 0.324 excluding all; 0.332 → 0.328 excluding Vogelherd only) while Aur-P2 is unchanged (0.125), indicating that figurines contribute marginally to within-group cohesion but do not create the community structure.

**Phase ordering is preserved.** The main-text connectivity contrast Aur-P1 > Aur-P2 (7.50 > 4.25) is unchanged under both exclusion scenarios (7.50 > 4.25 excluding all figurines; 7.40 > 4.25 excluding Vogelherd figurines only), preserving the key finding that the early phase is the more connected.

**The figurine effect is small and Vogelherd-specific.** Removing Vogelherd figurines alone (−1.3%) produces a similar, if slightly larger, effect than removing all 63 figurines globally (0%). Figurines at Hohle Fels, Geissenklösterle, Hohlenstein-Stadel, and La Ferrassie do not alter network structure. This indicates that although Vogelherd's figurine assemblage is unusually rich — 50 of 63 figurines — and contributes disproportionately to sign-type counts, its 123 remaining non-figurine objects still carry a sufficiently diverse sign repertoire to maintain network connectivity.

**Conclusion.** The main-text findings are robust to figurine exclusion. The Aur-P1 > Aur-P2 connectivity contrast, the two-group community structure, and the site membership of both phases are all preserved when figurines are removed. The concentration of figurines at Vogelherd does not bias the seriation or network results, and the broader-range group's connectivity within Aur-P1 is supported by non-figurine sign types. We note that modularity decreases slightly when figurines are excluded (Aur-P1: 0.332 → 0.324), suggesting that figurines contribute modestly to community cohesion — consistent with Bentz and Dutkiewicz's (2026) argument that figurines carry high-information sign sequences — but the communities themselves are defined by shared sign types across all object types.

# S8. Site Reclassification Sensitivity Analysis {#sec-s8}

## S8.1 Rationale

The main analysis assigns each site to an Aurignacian phase based on calibrated radiocarbon dates. However, several recent specialist reassessments demonstrate that radiocarbon dates alone are insufficient for phase attribution, and that the archaeological content of layers should take precedence:

- **Abri Pataud**: The lithic technology in levels 14–9 (carinated scraper bladelet cores, dual reduction systems) is diagnostic of the Early Aurignacian, not the Proto-Aurignacian, despite basal dates of ~41,200–39,500 cal BP that fall within the Proto-Aurignacian range [@Chiotti_2005; @Chiotti_Cretin_2011; @Higham_Abri_Pataud_2011]. The site is classified as Aurignacian I (Early) in the Périgord sequence.
- **La Ferrassie**: The Aurignacian at La Ferrassie begins in Layer 7, directly overlying the Châtelperronian (Layer 6). Talamo et al. (2020) classify this as Early Aurignacian based on carinated scrapers and wide Aurignacian blades. No split-base bone points (Proto-Aurignacian diagnostic) were found [@Delporte_et_al_1977; @Talamo_La_Ferrassie_2020]. Layer 7b has mixed Early/Recent Aurignacian components.
- **Mladeč**: The ~20 lithic artifacts include only one carinated end scraper. The 40 bone points with massive bases ("Mladeč-type") lack split bases and occur stratigraphically above split-based points at other Central European sites, placing them in the Evolved Aurignacian [@Oliva_2006]. Direct dates of ~31 ka ¹⁴C BP (~35–36 cal BP) are too young for Proto-Aurignacian [@Wild_et_al_2005].
- **Vogelherd**: Riek's 1931 excavation removed 500 m³ in 12 weeks with no screening, using large horizontal spits that did not follow geological horizons. Documented mixing includes 38 refit connections between Aurignacian layers IV and V, Neolithic burials disturbing the southwestern area, and ~2–3% of tools in the Aurignacian layers potentially deriving from other periods [@Schurch_Conard_2026].

This section tests two scenarios: (A) reclassifying Abri Pataud and La Ferrassie to the Early Aurignacian and Mladeč to the Evolved Aurignacian, following specialist technological attributions; and (B) additionally excluding Vogelherd entirely, given its documented stratigraphic mixing.

```{r}
# ── Analysis A: Reclassify sites to technologically correct phases ──────────
reclass_sites <- c("Abri Pataud", "La Ferrassie", "Mladeč")

signbase_reclass <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  mutate(time_period = case_when(
    site_name == "Abri Pataud" ~ "early_aurignacian",
    site_name == "La Ferrassie" ~ "early_aurignacian",
    site_name == "Mladeč" ~ "evolved_aurignacian",
    TRUE ~ time_period
  ))

lat_long_reclass <- signbase_reclass %>%
  dplyr::select(site_name, longitude, latitude) %>%
  distinct(site_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

proto_reclass   <- make_phase_data("proto_aurignacian", signbase_reclass, lat_long_reclass)
early_reclass   <- make_phase_data("early_aurignacian", signbase_reclass, lat_long_reclass)
evolved_reclass <- make_phase_data("evolved_aurignacian", signbase_reclass, lat_long_reclass)

proto_art_r   <- extract_artifact(proto_reclass)
early_art_r   <- extract_artifact(early_reclass)
evolved_art_r <- extract_artifact(evolved_reclass)

reclass_stats <- bind_rows(
  network_stats(proto_art_r, threshold = 0.2) %>% mutate(Phase = "Proto-Aurignacian"),
  network_stats(early_art_r, threshold = 0.2) %>% mutate(Phase = "Early Aurignacian"),
  network_stats(evolved_art_r, threshold = 0.2) %>% mutate(Phase = "Evolved Aurignacian")
) %>%
  mutate(Condition = "Reclassified") %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, Condition, n_sites, n_edges, density, mean_degree, transitivity, modularity)

# ── Analysis B: Additionally exclude Vogelherd ──────────────────────────────
exclude_sites <- c("Abri Pataud", "La Ferrassie", "Mladeč", "Vogelherd")

signbase_exclude <- signbase_full_clean %>%
  filter(!site_name %in% exclude_sites)

lat_long_exclude <- signbase_exclude %>%
  dplyr::select(site_name, longitude, latitude) %>%
  distinct(site_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

proto_excl   <- make_phase_data("proto_aurignacian", signbase_exclude, lat_long_exclude)
early_excl   <- make_phase_data("early_aurignacian", signbase_exclude, lat_long_exclude)
evolved_excl <- make_phase_data("evolved_aurignacian", signbase_exclude, lat_long_exclude)

proto_art_e   <- extract_artifact(proto_excl)
early_art_e   <- extract_artifact(early_excl)
evolved_art_e <- extract_artifact(evolved_excl)

excl_stats <- bind_rows(
  { ns <- network_stats(proto_art_e, threshold = 0.2); data.frame(Phase = "Proto-Aurignacian", n_sites = ns$n_sites, n_edges = ns$n_edges, density = ns$density, mean_degree = ns$mean_degree, transitivity = ns$transitivity, modularity = ns$modularity) },
  { ns <- network_stats(early_art_e, threshold = 0.2); data.frame(Phase = "Early Aurignacian", n_sites = ns$n_sites, n_edges = ns$n_edges, density = ns$density, mean_degree = ns$mean_degree, transitivity = ns$transitivity, modularity = ns$modularity) },
  { ns <- network_stats(evolved_art_e, threshold = 0.2); data.frame(Phase = "Evolved Aurignacian", n_sites = ns$n_sites, n_edges = ns$n_edges, density = ns$density, mean_degree = ns$mean_degree, transitivity = ns$transitivity, modularity = ns$modularity) }
) %>%
  mutate(Condition = "Excl. reclassified + Vogelherd") %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, Condition, n_sites, n_edges, density, mean_degree, transitivity, modularity)
```

## S8.2 Results

```{r}
# ── Baseline artifact data (original phase assignments) ────────────────────
proto_base   <- make_phase_data("proto_aurignacian", signbase_full_clean, lat_long_df)
early_base   <- make_phase_data("early_aurignacian", signbase_full_clean, lat_long_df)
evolved_base <- make_phase_data("evolved_aurignacian", signbase_full_clean, lat_long_df)

proto_art   <- extract_artifact(proto_base)
early_art   <- extract_artifact(early_base)
evolved_art <- extract_artifact(evolved_base)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reclass-comparison
#| tbl-cap: "Network statistics under three conditions: baseline (all sites as originally assigned), reclassified (Abri Pataud and La Ferrassie moved to Early Aurignacian, Mladeč moved to Evolved Aurignacian), and excluded (reclassified sites plus Vogelherd removed entirely). Threshold = 0.2, Jaccard similarity."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom

baseline_reclass <- bind_rows(
  network_stats(proto_art, threshold = 0.2) %>% mutate(Phase = "Proto-Aurignacian"),
  network_stats(early_art, threshold = 0.2) %>% mutate(Phase = "Early Aurignacian"),
  network_stats(evolved_art, threshold = 0.2) %>% mutate(Phase = "Evolved Aurignacian")
) %>%
  mutate(Condition = "Baseline") %>%
  dplyr::select(Phase, Condition, n_sites, n_edges, density, mean_degree, transitivity, modularity)

all_reclass <- bind_rows(baseline_reclass, reclass_stats, excl_stats)

kable(all_reclass,
      col.names = c("Phase", "Condition", "Sites", "Edges", "Density",
                    "Mean degree", "Transitivity", "Modularity"),
      digits = 3,
      align = "lllcccccc")
```

```{r}
# ── Compute % change from baseline for prose ────────────────────────────────
reclass_pct <- all_reclass %>%
  group_by(Phase) %>%
  mutate(baseline_md = first(mean_degree),
         pct_change = round((mean_degree - baseline_md) / baseline_md * 100, 1)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

### Reclassification effects by phase

**Proto-Aurignacian.** Reclassifying Abri Pataud, La Ferrassie, and Mladeč reduces the Proto from `r all_reclass$n_sites[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$n_sites[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]` sites and from `r all_reclass$n_edges[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$n_edges[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]` edges. Mean degree drops from `r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]` (`r reclass_pct$pct_change[reclass_pct$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & reclass_pct$Condition == "Reclassified"]`%), and modularity increases from `r all_reclass$modularity[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$modularity[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & reclass_pct$Condition == "Reclassified"]`. The loss of La Ferrassie — the most connected node in the baseline Proto-Aurignacian network — is the primary driver of this decline.

**Early Aurignacian.** Adding Abri Pataud and La Ferrassie increases the Early from `r all_reclass$n_sites[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$n_sites[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]` sites and from `r all_reclass$n_edges[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$n_edges[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]` edges. Mean degree rises from `r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]` (`r reclass_pct$pct_change[reclass_pct$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & reclass_pct$Condition == "Reclassified"]`%).

**Evolved Aurignacian.** Adding Mladeč increases the Evolved from `r all_reclass$n_sites[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$n_sites[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]` sites and from `r all_reclass$n_edges[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$n_edges[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]` edges. Mean degree rises from `r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]` to `r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]` (`r reclass_pct$pct_change[reclass_pct$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & reclass_pct$Condition == "Reclassified"]`%).

## S8.3 Phase-Ordering Reversal

The most consequential finding is that **the phase ordering of connectivity reverses under reclassification**:

| Condition | Ordering |
|-----------|----------|
| Baseline | Proto (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]`) > Early (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]`) > Evolved (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Baseline"]`) |
| Reclassified | Early (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]`) > Evolved (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]`) > Proto (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Reclassified"]`) |

Under the reclassified assignments, the Early Aurignacian becomes the most connected phase, the Evolved Aurignacian is intermediate, and the Proto-Aurignacian — which loses La Ferrassie, its primary hub — becomes the least connected. This ordering is preserved when Vogelherd is additionally excluded (Analysis B): Early (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Excl. reclassified + Vogelherd"]`) > Evolved (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Excl. reclassified + Vogelherd"]`) > Proto (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Excl. reclassified + Vogelherd"]`).

## S8.4 Interpretation

The reclassification analysis reveals that the main-text finding — that the Proto-Aurignacian was the most connected phase — is **contingent on the assignment of La Ferrassie to the Proto-Aurignacian**. La Ferrassie contributes 22 objects to the Proto-Aurignacian and serves as the network's primary hub. When it is reassigned to the Early Aurignacian (where its lithic technology places it: carinated scrapers, wide Aurignacian blades, no split-base points; Talamo et al. 2020; Delporte et al. 1977), the Proto-Aurignacian loses its hub structure and its mean degree drops below both the Early and Evolved phases.

This does not invalidate the main-text analysis, but it necessitates a qualification: **the Proto-Aurignacian's apparent connectivity advantage depends on radiocarbon-based phase assignments that specialist lithic analysis contradicts.** The three-phase ordering Proto > Early > Evolved should be treated as a hypothesis consistent with one plausible phase assignment, not as a demonstrated fact. Two alternative orderings — Early > Evolved > Proto (reclassified) and Early > Proto > Evolved (intermediate scenarios) — are equally consistent with the data under different but archaeologically justified phase attributions.

What remains robust across all conditions is the **two-group community structure**: restricted-range and broader-range assemblages persist in every phase regardless of which sites are included. The perMANOVA results confirming significant group separation in sign composition are also expected to hold, since the reclassified sites (Abri Pataud, La Ferrassie, Mladeč) belong to the restricted-range group in the Proto-Aurignacian and would occupy analogous positions in their new phases. The broader conclusion that Aurignacian communities maintained differentiated sign repertoires — possibly reflecting variation in social structure — is not affected by the reclassification.

The exclusion analysis (Analysis B) shows that removing all four problematic sites (Abri Pataud, La Ferrassie, Mladeč, Vogelherd) further reduces connectivity across all phases but preserves the reclassified ordering: the Early Aurignacian (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Early Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Excl. reclassified + Vogelherd"]`°) remains the most connected, followed by the Evolved (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Evolved Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Excl. reclassified + Vogelherd"]`°) and the Proto (`r all_reclass$mean_degree[all_reclass$Phase == "Proto-Aurignacian" & all_reclass$Condition == "Excl. reclassified + Vogelherd"]`°). The fact that the Early Aurignacian retains the highest connectivity even without Vogelherd — which contributes 50 figurines and 114 non-figurine objects — indicates that its network structure is driven by multiple sites (Hohle Fels, Solutré, Castanet, Cellier, Blanchard) rather than by a single outlier assemblage.
